value.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
value.en: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).
value.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

value.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
value.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
value.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

value.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
value.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
value.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.

value.zh: 迎常道鄉公於東武陽，遷中撫軍，進封新昌鄉侯。
value.en: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinchang.
value.literal: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.

value.zh: 及晉國建，立爲世子，拜撫軍大將軍，開府、副貳相國。
value.en: When the Jin state was founded, he was established as heir apparent, appointed Great General Who Pacifies the Army with an office of his own, and made second-in-command assisting the Minister of State.
value.literal: When the state of Jin was founded he was established as heir apparent, appointed great general who pacifies the army with independent command, and served as deputy to the minister of state.

value.zh: 十一月，大舉伐吳，遣鎮軍將軍、琅邪王伷出涂中，[24]安東將軍王渾出江西，建威將軍王戎出武昌，平南將軍胡奮出夏口，鎮南大將軍杜預出江陵，龍驤將軍王濬、廣武將軍唐彬率巴蜀之卒浮江而下，東西凡二十餘萬。
value.en: In the eleventh month: the conquest of Wu opened on every vector—Sima Zhou from Tu, Wang Hun from the north bank, Wang Rong, Hu Fen, Du Yu, and a river fleet under Wang Jun and Tang Bin—over two hundred thousand soldiers [24].
value.literal: In the eleventh month a great campaign was launched against Wu: Sima Zhou, general who guards the army and king of Langye, went out from Tu; Wang Hun, general who guards the east, from west of the river; Wang Rong, general who displays might, from Wuchang; Hu Fen, general who pacifies the south, from Xiakou; Du Yu, great general who guards the south, from Jiangling; Wang Jun, general who displays dragon prowess, and Tang Bin, general who displays martial breadth, led Ba–Shu troops down the Yangzi—more than two hundred thousand men on the eastern and western axes combined [24].

value.zh: 以太尉賈充爲大都督，行冠軍將軍楊濟爲副，總統眾軍。
value.en: Jia Chong, Grand Commandant, was made Grand Commander-in-chief; Yang Ji, acting General Who Displays Champion Prowess, served as his deputy, and together they commanded all the armies.
value.literal: Grand commandant Jia Chong was made supreme commander, with acting general who displays champion prowess Yang Ji as deputy, commanding all hosts.

value.zh: 二月戊午，王濬、唐彬等克丹楊城。
value.en: Second month, wuwu: the river fleet seized Danyang.
value.literal: On the day wuwu of the second month Wang Jun, Tang Bin, and others took Danyang city.

value.zh: 庚申，又克西陵，殺西陵都督、鎮軍將軍留憲，[25]征南將軍成璩，西陵監鄭廣。
value.en: Gengshen: Xiling fell; Liu Xian, Cheng Qu, and Zheng Guang died defending it [25].
value.literal: On the day gengshen they also took Xiling, killing Xiling commander and general who guards the army Liu Xian [25], general who campaigns south Cheng Qu, and Xiling intendant Zheng Guang.

value.zh: 壬戌，濬又克夷道樂鄉城，殺夷道監陸晏、水軍都督陸景。
value.en: Renxu: Wang Jun pushed to Yidao and Lexiang and killed Lu Yan and Lu Jing.
value.literal: On the day renxu Jun further took Yidao and Lexiang towns, killing Yidao intendant Lu Yan and commander of the navy Lu Jing.

value.zh: 甲戌，杜預克江陵，斬吳江陵督伍延；
value.en: Jiaxu: Du Yu entered Jiangling and executed Wu Yan;
value.literal: On the day jiaxu Du Yu took Jiangling and beheaded Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan;

value.zh: 平南將軍胡奮克江安。
value.en: Hu Fen secured Jiang’an.
value.literal: General who pacifies the south Hu Fen took Jiang’an.

value.zh: 於是諸軍並進，樂鄉、荊門諸戍相次來降。
value.en: Fort after fort—Lexiang, Jingmen—raised white flags.
value.literal: Thereupon all armies advanced together, and the garrisons at Lexiang, Jingmen, and others surrendered in succession.

value.zh: 乙亥，以濬爲都督益、梁二州諸軍事，復下詔曰：「濬、彬東下，掃除巴丘，與胡奮、王戎共平夏口、武昌，順流長騖，直造秣陵，與奮、戎審量其宜。
value.en: On yihai, Wang Jun was made commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yi and Liang provinces, and an edict was again issued, saying, "Jun and Bin shall go east, sweep away Baqiu, and together with Hu Fen and Wang Rong pacify Xiakou and Wuchang, drive swiftly down the current, and go straight to Moling; with Fen and Rong, carefully measure what is appropriate.
value.literal: On the day yihai Wang Jun was appointed supervisor of all military affairs of Yi and Liang provinces, and an edict further said: “When Jun and Bin sail east, clear Baqiu, join Hu Fen and Wang Rong to pacify Xiakou and Wuchang, then drive straight down the stream to Moling with Fen and Rong coordinating as fits.

value.zh: 杜預當鎮靜零、桂，懷輯衡陽。
value.en: Du Yu was to hold the southern Jing pocket and win over Hengyang.
value.literal: Du Yu shall keep calm over Ling and Gui and soothe Hengyang.

value.zh: 大兵既過，荊州南境固當傳檄而定，預當分萬人給濬，七千給彬。
value.en: After the main thrust, Du Yu was to feed ten thousand troops to Wang Jun and seven thousand to Tang Bin.
value.literal: Once the great army has passed, the southern marches of Jing ought to be settled by proclamation alone; Yu shall detach ten thousand men to Jun and seven thousand to Bin.

value.zh: 夏口既平，奮宜以七千人給濬。
value.en: When Xiakou fell, Hu Fen was to shift seven thousand soldiers to Wang Jun.
value.literal: Once Xiakou is pacified, Fen should give seven thousand men to Jun.

value.zh: 武昌既了，戎當以六千人增彬。
value.en: After Wuchang, Wang Rong was to reinforce Tang Bin with six thousand.
value.literal: Once Wuchang is settled, Rong should add six thousand men to Bin.

value.zh: 太尉充移屯項，總督諸方。」
value.en: Jia Chong would move headquarters to Xiang and coordinate all theaters.”
value.literal: Grand commandant Chong shall shift his camp to Xiang and oversee every front.”

value.zh: 濬進破夏口、武昌，遂泛舟東下，所至皆平。
value.en: Wang Jun smashed the river defenses and swept downstream unopposed.
value.literal: Jun advanced, broke Xiakou and Wuchang, then sailed east; wherever he went it was pacified.

value.zh: 王渾、周浚與吳丞相張悌戰于版橋，大破之，斬悌及其將孫震、沈瑩，傳首洛陽。
value.en: At Banqiao Wang Hun and Zhou Jun killed Zhang Ti and his generals Sun Zhen and Shen Ying and shipped the heads north.
value.literal: Wang Hun, Zhou Jun, and Wu chancellor Zhang Ti fought at Banqiao; they crushed him, beheaded Ti and his generals Sun Zhen and Shen Ying, and sent the heads to Luoyang.

value.zh: 孫皓窮蹙請降，送璽綬於琅邪王伷。
value.en: Sun Hao capitulated, handing the imperial seal to Sima Zhou.
value.literal: Sun Hao, driven to extremity, asked to surrender and sent the seal and cord to king Zhou of Langye.

value.zh: 丙寅，帝臨軒大會，引皓升殿，群臣咸稱萬歲。
value.en: Bingyin [29]: the emperor came to the hall for a great assembly, led Sun Hao up into the hall, and the ministers all cried 'ten thousand years.'
value.literal: On the day bingyin [29] the emperor came to the gallery for a great assembly, led Hao up the hall, and the host of ministers cried “ten thousand years.”

value.zh: 丁卯，薦酃淥酒于太廟。
value.en: Dingmao: Linglu wine was poured for the ancestors.
value.literal: On the day dingmao fine wine from Linglu was offered in the grand temple.

value.zh: 郡國六雹，傷秋稼。
value.en: Six more provinces reported hail damage.
value.literal: Six commanderies and principalities were struck by hail that injured the autumn crop.

value.zh: 庚午，詔諸士卒年六十以上罷歸于家。
value.en: Gengwu: veterans over sixty were sent home.
value.literal: On the day gengwu an edict ordered soldiers aged sixty and above dismissed home.

value.zh: 庚辰，以王濬爲輔國大將軍、襄陽侯，杜預當陽侯，王戎安豐侯，唐彬上庸侯，賈充、琅邪王伷以下增封。
value.en: Gengchen: Wang Jun was made great general who assists the state and marquis of Xiangyang, Du Yu marquis of Dangyang, Wang Rong marquis of Anfeng, Tang Bin marquis of Shangyong, and Jia Chong, Sima Zhou the king of Langye, and those below them received increased fiefs.
value.literal: On the day gengchen Wang Jun was made great general who assists the state and marquis of Xiangyang, Du Yu marquis of Dangyang, Wang Rong marquis of Anfeng, Tang Bin marquis of Shangyong, and Jia Chong, king Zhou of Langye, and those below received increased fiefs.

value.zh: 於是論功行封，賜公卿以下帛各有差。
value.en: Silks followed to the whole bureaucracy graded by service.
value.literal: Thereupon merit was weighed and enfeoffments granted, and silks were bestowed on the dukes and ministers downward, each according to difference.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 秋八月壬午，立廣陵王遹爲皇太子，以中書監何劭爲太子太師，吏部尚書王戎爲太子太傅，衛將軍楊濟爲太子太保。
value.en: In autumn, on the renwu day of the eighth month, Sima Yu, prince of Guangling, was named crown prince; He Shao became his grand preceptor, Wang Rong his grand tutor, and Yang Ji his grand guardian.
value.literal: In autumn, on the renwu day of the eighth month, Prince Sima You of Guangling was established as crown prince; Director of the Secretariat He Shao was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent; Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Rong was made grand tutor of the heir apparent; General of the Guards Yang Ji was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

value.zh: 遣南中郎將石崇、射聲校尉胡奕、長水校尉趙俊、揚烈將軍趙歡將屯兵四出。
value.en: Shi Chong, Hu Yi, Zhao Jun, and Zhao Huan were sent out at the head of garrison forces in every direction.
value.literal: General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household Shi Chong, Colonel of the Sound of Shooting Hu Yi, Colonel of the Long River Zhao Jun, and General Who Displays Ferocity Zhao Huan were dispatched leading garrison troops in four directions.

value.zh: 夏四月癸亥，以征東將軍、梁王肜爲征西大將軍、都督關西諸軍事，太子少傅阮坦爲平東將軍、監青徐二州諸軍事。
value.en: Prince Rong of Liang was shifted from the eastern to the western theater as area commander beyond the passes, while Ruan Tan was sent to pacify the east and oversee the armies of Qing and Xu.
value.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the guihai day, General Who Conquers the East, Prince Xiong of Liang, was made general-in-chief who conquers the west and area commander for all military affairs west of the passes; Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Ruan Tan was made general who pacifies the east and overseer of military affairs in Qing and Xu provinces.

value.zh: 己巳，以太子太傅王戎爲尚書右僕射。
value.en: Wang Rong moved from tutoring the heir apparent to the right vice directorship of the secretariat.
value.literal: On the jisi day, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wang Rong was made right vice director of the secretariat.

value.zh: 九月，以尚書右僕射王戎爲司徒，太子太師何劭爲尚書左僕射。
value.en: Wang Rong advanced from right vice director to minister of education, and He Shao from the heir apparent’s grand preceptor to left vice director of the secretariat in the ninth month.
value.literal: In the ninth month, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Rong was made minister of education; Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent He Shao was made left vice director of the secretariat.

value.zh: 秋七月丙申朔，右衛將軍陳眕以詔召百僚入殿中，因勒兵討成都王穎。
value.en: On the bingshen new moon of autumn’s seventh month, General of the Right Guards Chen Zhen used an edict to summon the hundred officials into the palace hall, then led troops against Prince Ying of Chengdu.
value.literal: In autumn, on the bingshen new moon of the seventh month, General of the Right Guards Chen Zhen used an edict to summon the hundred officials into the palace, then led troops to attack Prince Ying of Chengdu.

value.zh: 戊戌，大赦，復皇后羊氏及皇太子覃。
value.en: Empress Yang and Crown Prince Tan were restored on wuxu under a general amnesty.
value.literal: On the wuxu day a general amnesty restored Empress Yang and Crown Prince Tan.

value.zh: 己亥，司徒王戎、東海王越、高密王簡、平昌公模、吳王晏、豫章王熾、襄陽王範、右僕射荀藩等奉帝北征。
value.en: On jihai Wang Rong, Prince Yue, Prince Jian, Sima Mo, Prince Yan, Prince Chi, Prince Fan, and Xun Fan convoyed the emperor north.
value.literal: On the jihai day Minister of Education Wang Rong, Prince Yue of Donghai, Prince Jian of Gaomi, Duke Mo of Pingchang, Prince Yan of Wu, Prince Chi of Yuzhang, Prince Fan of Xiangyang, and Right Vice Director Xun Fan and others escorted the emperor on a northern expedition.

value.zh: 至安陽，眾十餘萬，穎遣其將石超距戰。
value.en: The army swelled past a hundred thousand at Anyang, where Prince Ying sent Shi Chao to bar the road.
value.literal: When they reached Anyang the host exceeded one hundred thousand; Ying dispatched his general Shi Chao to resist in battle.

value.zh: 己未，六軍敗績于蕩陰，矢及乘輿，百官分散，侍中嵇紹死之。
value.en: At Dangyin on jiwei the imperial army collapsed, arrows riddled the imperial coach, the courtiers fled, and Ji Shao died shielding the throne.
value.literal: On the jiwei day the six armies were defeated at Dangyin; arrows reached the imperial carriage; the hundred officials scattered; Palace Attendant Ji Shao died in the engagement.

value.zh: 帝傷頰，中三矢，亡六璽。
value.en: The sovereign took three hits in the cheek and lost six of the dynasty’s jade seals in the rout.
value.literal: The emperor was wounded in the cheek, struck by three arrows, and lost six of the imperial seals.

value.zh: 帝遂幸超軍，餒甚，超進水，左右奉秋桃。
value.en: Starving, he fell into Shi Chao’s lines; Chao gave him water while attendants found late peaches.
value.literal: The emperor thereupon visited Chao’s camp, was extremely hungry; Chao advanced water, and attendants offered autumn peaches.

value.zh: 超遣弟熙奉帝之鄴，穎帥群官迎謁道左。
value.en: Shi Chao’s brother Shi Xi escorted the emperor toward Ye, where Prince Ying knelt with his entire staff along the road.
value.literal: Chao sent his younger brother Xi to convoy the emperor to Ye; Ying led the host of officials to bow in welcome by the roadside.

value.zh: 帝下輿涕泣，其夕幸于穎軍。
value.en: He stepped down from the coach in tears and spent the night in Prince Ying’s encampment.
value.literal: The emperor alighted from the carriage weeping; that evening he lodged in Ying’s camp.

value.zh: 穎府有九錫之儀，陳留王送貂蟬文衣鶡尾，明日，乃備法駕幸于鄴，唯豫章王熾、司徒王戎、僕射荀藩從。
value.en: Prince Ying’s compound already displayed the nine-bestowal regalia; the prince of Chenliu sent the full accoutrements of investiture, and on the following day the emperor entered Ye with complete state panoply, attended only by Prince Chi, Wang Rong, and Xun Fan.
value.literal: Ying’s headquarters held the regalia for the nine bestowals; the Prince of Chenliu presented sable-cicada insignia, patterned robes, and pheasant-tail pennants; the next day the full imperial equipage was prepared and proceeded to Ye; only Prince Chi of Yuzhang, Minister Wang Rong, and Vice Director Xun Fan accompanied.

value.zh: 庚申，大赦，改元爲建武。
value.en: The reign was renamed Jianwu on gengshen amid another general amnesty.
value.literal: On the gengshen day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jianwu.

value.zh: 十二月丁亥，詔曰：「天禍晉邦，冢嗣莫繼。
value.en: On the dinghai day in the twelfth month an edict began: “Heaven scourges Jin, and no son of mine survives to succeed.
value.literal: On the dinghai day of the twelfth month an edict stated: “Heaven has punished the Jin state; no heir succeeds.

value.zh: 成都王穎自在儲貳，政績虧損，四海失望，不可承重，其以王還第。
value.en: Prince Ying proved unfit while heir apparent and has forfeited the trust of the realm, so he must be stripped of the succession and sent home to his fief.
value.literal: Prince Ying of Chengdu, while heir, failed in government; within the four seas hope was disappointed; he cannot bear the heavy charge; let him return to his residence as a prince.

value.zh: 豫章王熾先帝愛子，令問日新，四海注意，今以爲皇太弟，以隆我晉邦。
value.en: Prince Chi of Yuzhang, the late emperor’s favorite, grows in reputation every day, and he shall be named imperial younger brother and heir to steady the house of Jin.
value.literal: Prince Chi of Yuzhang was the late emperor’s beloved son; his fair fame grows daily; within the four seas all eyes turn to him; now let him be made imperial younger brother and heir to uplift our Jin state.

value.zh: 以司空越爲太傅，與太宰顒夾輔朕躬。
value.en: Minister of Works Prince Yue is appointed grand tutor to work beside Grand Steward Yong in guiding the throne.
value.literal: Let Minister of Works Yue be made grand tutor, together with Grand Steward Yong to flank and assist my person.

value.zh: 司徒王戎參錄朝政，光祿大夫王衍爲尚書左僕射。
value.en: Wang Rong shall join in supervising policy, and Wang Yan shall take the left vice directorship of the secretariat.
value.literal: Let Minister of Education Wang Rong participate in recording court governance; Household Grandee Wang Yan is made left vice director of the secretariat.

value.zh: 安南將軍虓、安北將軍浚、平北將軍騰各守本鎮。
value.en: Generals Xiao, Jun, and Teng are ordered to hold their existing commands.
value.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Xiao, General Who Pacifies the North Jun, and General Who Pacifies the North Teng each guard their original garrisons.

value.zh: 高密王簡爲鎮南將軍，領司隸校尉，權鎮洛陽；
value.en: Prince Jian of Gaomi becomes general who guards the south and acting metropolitan superintendent at Luoyang.
value.literal: Prince Jian of Gaomi is made general who guards the south, concurrently metropolitan superintendent, acting in authority at Luoyang;

value.zh: 東中郎將模爲寧北將軍、都督冀州，鎮于鄴；
value.en: Sima Mo moves to general who guards the north with Ji Province command, based at Ye.
value.literal: General of the Household Gentlemen of the East Mo is made general who guards the north and area commander for Ji Province, stationed at Ye;

value.zh: 鎮南大將軍劉弘領荊州，以鎮南土。
value.en: Liu Hong, general-in-chief who guards the south, keeps order in Jing Province.
value.literal: General-in-chief Who Guards the South Liu Hong holds Jing Province to secure the south.

value.zh: 周馥、繆胤各還本部，百官皆復職。
value.en: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin go back to their posts, and every minister returns to duty.
value.literal: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin each return to their original commands; the hundred officials all resume their posts.

value.zh: 齊王冏前應還第，長沙王乂輕陷重刑，封其子紹爲樂平縣王，以奉其嗣。
value.en: Prince Jiong ought long ago to have been sent to his domain, and Prince Yi suffered a cruel death, so enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping to preserve his line.
value.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi should earlier have returned to his residence; Prince Yi of Changsha was lightly subjected to heavy punishment; enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping county to continue his line.

value.zh: 自頃戎車屢征，勞費人力，供御之物皆減三分之二，戶調田租三分減一。
value.en: Because armies have marched again and again, palace supplies are cut by two-thirds, and the poll tax and land rent are each reduced by a third.
value.literal: Recently war-chariots have repeatedly marched, exhausting men and resources; articles for the imperial household are all reduced by two-thirds; household levies and field rent are each reduced by one-third.

value.zh: 蠲除苛政，愛人務本。
value.en: Harsh statutes are swept away so the people may return to their fields.
value.literal: Harsh government is remitted; the people are cherished and the root is sought.

value.zh: 清通之後，當還東京。」
value.en: Once peace is restored, the court will return to Luoyang.”
value.literal: After the realm is cleared and at peace, we shall return to the eastern capital.”

value.zh: 大赦，改元。
value.en: The edict ended with a general amnesty and a new reign title.
value.literal: A general amnesty; the era name was changed.

value.zh: 以河間王顒都督中外諸軍事。
value.en: Prince Yong of Hejian received overall command of every army.
value.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian was made area commander for all military affairs within and without.

value.zh: 六月甲子，侍中、司徒、安豐侯王戎薨。
value.en: On jiazi in the sixth month, Wang Rong, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, and Marquis of Anfeng, died.
value.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Wang Rong, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, and Marquis of Anfeng, died.

value.zh: 隴西太守韓稚攻秦州刺史張輔，殺之。
value.en: Han Zhi, Administrator of Longxi, attacked and killed Zhang Fu, Inspector of Qinzhou.
value.literal: Han Zhi, Administrator of Longxi, attacked Zhang Fu, Inspector of Qinzhou, and killed him.

value.zh: 李雄僭即帝位，國號蜀。
value.en: Li Xiong usurped the imperial title and named his state Shu.
value.literal: Li Xiong usurped the imperial position and named his state Shu.

value.zh: 陳騫
value.en: Chen Qian
value.literal: Chen Qian

value.zh: =楷字叔則。
value.en: Pei Kai, whose courtesy name was Shuzé,
value.literal: Kai, courtesy name Shuzé.

value.zh: 父徽，魏冀州刺史。
value.en: His father Hui had been Governor of Jizhou under Wei.
value.literal: His father Hui had been Governor of Jizhou under Wei.

value.zh: 楷明悟有識量，弱冠知名，尤精《老》、《易》，少與王戎齊名。
value.en: Celebrated before twenty, he mastered the Daoist classics alongside Wang Rong.
value.literal: Kai was lucid and discerning, with breadth of judgment; before age twenty he was famous, especially in the Laozi and Changes, and was paired in renown with Wang Rong.

value.zh: 鍾會薦之于文帝，辟相國掾，遷尚書郎。
value.en: Zhong Hui's referral brought him into Sima Zhao's bureau and the secretariat.
value.literal: Zhong Hui recommended him to Emperor Wen; Kai became aide to the minister of state and rose to gentleman of the palace secretariat.

value.zh: 賈充改定律令，以楷為定科郎。
value.en: Jia Chong's law revision named Kai specialist for codifying clauses.
value.literal: When Jia Chong revised statutes, Kai served as the drafter charged with fixing each legal article.

value.zh: 事畢，詔楷於御前執讀，平議當否。
value.en: At court he read the new code aloud for imperial scrutiny.
value.literal: When the code was done, an edict ordered Kai to read it aloud before the throne and debate whether each clause fit.

value.zh: 楷善宣吐，左右屬目，聽者忘倦。
value.en: His exposition captivated the hall.
value.literal: Kai spoke with luminous clarity; attendants hung on every word and listeners forgot fatigue.

value.zh: 武帝為撫軍，妙選僚采，以楷為參軍事。
value.en: Sima Yan made him staff adviser during the princely generalship.
value.literal: While Emperor Wu still served as General Who Supports the Army, he chose Kai as military administrator.

value.zh: 吏部郎缺，文帝問其人於鍾會。
value.en: Sima Zhao asked Zhong Hui who should head personnel.
value.literal: The personnel director post stood empty; Emperor Wen asked Zhong Hui whom to appoint.

value.zh: 會曰：「裴楷清通，王戎簡要，皆其選也。」
value.en: "Pei Kai or Wang Rong," said Zhong Hui, "both fit."
value.literal: Hui replied: "Pei Kai is lucid and penetrating; Wang Rong concise and essential—either suits the post."

value.zh: 於是以楷為吏部郎。
value.en: Kai received the appointment.
value.literal: Thereupon Kai became Director of Personnel.

value.zh: 楷長子輿先娶亮女，女適衛瓘子，楷慮內難未已，求出外鎮，除安南將軍、假節、都督荊州諸軍事，垂當發而瑋果矯詔誅亮、瓘。
value.en: Marriage ties to both factions drove Kai toward Jingzhou—Wei's forged orders struck first.
value.literal: Kai's heir Yu had first married Sima Liang's daughter, and Kai's daughter was married to a son of Wei Guan—fearing civil war Kai sought a province; made General Who Pacifies the South, with staff, commanding Jingzhou military affairs—just as he prepared to march, Wei forged an edict killing Liang and Guan.

value.zh: 瑋以楷前奪己中候，又與亮、瓘婚親，密遣討楷。
value.en: Wei sent killers after Kai for family links to his victims.
value.literal: Wei because Kai had earlier displaced him from Central Commander and was also marriage kin to Liang and Guan secretly sent forces against Kai.

value.zh: 楷素知瑋有望于己，聞有變，單車入城，匿于妻父王渾家，與亮小子一夜八徙，故得免難。
value.en: He dodged patrols by hiding with Wang Hun and Liang's orphan.
value.literal: Kai had always known Wei bore him ill will; hearing of the upheaval, he drove alone into the city and hid in his father-in-law Wang Hun's house; with Liang's youngest son he moved eight times in one night—thus he escaped harm.

value.zh: 瑋既伏誅，以楷為中書令，加侍中，與張華、王戎並管機要。
value.en: Wei fell and Kai joined Zhang Hua and Wang Rong at power's core.
value.literal: After Wei died Kai directed the palace secretariat with Zhang Hua and Wang Rong.

value.zh: 楷有渴利疾，不樂處勢。
value.en: Diabetes-like thirst made central office unbearable.
value.literal: Kai suffered wasting thirst and loathed heavy responsibility.

value.zh: 王渾為楷請曰：「楷受先帝拔擢之恩，復蒙陛下寵遇，誠竭節之秋也。
value.en: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.
value.literal: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.

value.zh: 然楷性不競於物，昔為常侍，求出為河內太守；
value.en: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.
value.literal: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.

value.zh: 後為侍中，復求出為河南尹；
value.en: Later, when he was Palace Attendant, he again sought to go out as Governor of Henan.
value.literal: Later, when he was Palace Attendant, he again sought to go out as Governor of Henan.

value.zh: 與楊駿不平，求為衛尉；
value.en: When he was not on good terms with Yang Jun, he sought to become Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.
value.literal: When he was not on good terms with Yang Jun, he sought to become Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.

value.zh: 及轉東宮，班在時類之下，安於淡退，有識有以見其心也。
value.en: When he was transferred to the Eastern Palace, his rank was below those of his time and class, yet he was at ease in plain withdrawal. Those with understanding had means to see his mind.
value.literal: When he was transferred to the Eastern Palace, his rank was below those of his time and class, yet he was at ease in plain withdrawal. Those with understanding had means to see his mind.

value.zh: 楷今委頓，臣深憂之。
value.en: Kai is now worn down, and I am deeply worried about him.
value.literal: Kai is now worn down, and I am deeply worried about him.

value.zh: 光祿勳缺，以為可用。
value.en: The office of Chamberlain for the Splendid Blessings is vacant, and I think he can be used there.
value.literal: The office of Chamberlain for the Splendid Blessings is vacant, and I think he can be used there.

value.zh: 今張華在中書，王戎在尚書，足舉其契，無為復令楷入，名臣不多，當見將養，不違其志，要其遠濟之益。」
value.en: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat, and Wang Rong is in the Department of State Affairs; they are enough to raise what fits. There is no need to make Kai enter again. Eminent ministers are not many, and he should be cared for and nourished, without violating his will, so as to seek his long-range benefit."
value.literal: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat, and Wang Rong is in the Department of State Affairs; they are enough to raise what fits. There is no need to make Kai enter again. Eminent ministers are not many, and he should be cared for and nourished, without violating his will, so as to seek his long-range benefit."

value.zh: 不聽，就加光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
value.en: The throne instead piled on Household Grandee and three-duke parity.
value.literal: [The emperor] did not listen; [Kai] was additionally given Household Grandee and allowed to maintain a separate headquarters with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.

value.zh: 及疾篤，詔遣黃門郎王衍省疾，楷回眸矚之曰：「竟未相識。」
value.en: When his illness became severe, the edict sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yan to inspect his illness. Kai turned his eyes back and gazed at him, saying, "In the end, we never came to know one another."
value.literal: When his illness became severe, the edict sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yan to inspect his illness. Kai turned his eyes back and gazed at him, saying, "In the end, we never came to know one another."

value.zh: 衍深歎其神俊。
value.en: Yan stood awed by that dying brilliance.
value.literal: Yan deeply sighed at his spiritual brilliance.

value.zh: 安平獻王孚
value.en: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.
value.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).

value.zh: 河間王顒表立成都王穎為太弟，為王浚所破，挾天子還洛陽。
value.en: Yong's heir plot collapsed under Wang Jun forcing return east.
value.literal: Prince of Hejian Yong memorialized establishing Chengdu Prince Ying heir-apparent; defeated by Wang Jun he escorted Son of Heaven back Luoyang.

value.zh: 虓與東平王楙、鎮東將軍周馥等上言曰：自湣懷被害，皇儲不建，委重前相，輒失臣節。
value.en: Xiao, together with King Mao of Dongping, General Who Guards the East Zhou Fu, and others, submitted words, saying: Since Minhuai was harmed, the imperial heir has not been established. Weighty responsibility was entrusted to the former minister, and he then lost the duty of a subject.
value.literal: Xiao, together with King Mao of Dongping, General Who Guards the East Zhou Fu, and others, submitted words, saying: Since Minhuai was harmed, the imperial heir has not been established. Weighty responsibility was entrusted to the former minister, and he then lost the duty of a subject.

value.zh: 是以前年太宰與臣，永惟社稷之貳，不可久空，所以共啟成都王穎，以為國副。
value.en: Therefore in the previous year the Grand Steward and we your servants long considered that the deputy of the altars of soil and grain could not remain vacant for long, and for this reason we jointly proposed King Ying of Chengdu to be deputy to the state.
value.literal: Therefore in the previous year the Grand Steward and we your servants long considered that the deputy of the altars of soil and grain could not remain vacant for long, and for this reason we jointly proposed King Ying of Chengdu to be deputy to the state.

value.zh: 受重之後，而弗克負荷。
value.en: After receiving this weighty charge, he was unable to bear it.
value.literal: After receiving this weighty charge, he was unable to bear it.

value.zh: 「小人勿用」，而以為腹心。
value.en: "Do not employ petty men," yet he made them his trusted intimates.
value.literal: "Do not employ petty men," yet he made them his trusted intimates.

value.zh: 骨肉宜敦，而猜佻薦至，險詖宜遠，而讒說殄行。
value.en: Flesh-and-blood kin should have been treated with thick affection, yet suspicion and frivolity arrived repeatedly; dangerous and slanting men should have been kept distant, yet slanderous talk destroyed conduct.
value.literal: Flesh-and-blood kin should have been treated with thick affection, yet suspicion and frivolity arrived repeatedly; dangerous and slanting men should have been kept distant, yet slanderous talk destroyed conduct.

value.zh: 此皆臣等不聰不明，失所宗賴。
value.en: All this was because we your servants were neither perceptive nor clear-sighted and lost the one on whom we relied.
value.literal: All this was because we your servants were neither perceptive nor clear-sighted and lost the one on whom we relied.

value.zh: 遂令陛下謬于降授，雖戮臣等，不足以謝天下。
value.en: We then caused Your Majesty to err in lowering and granting rank; even if you executed us, it would not be enough to apologize to all under Heaven.
value.literal: We then caused Your Majesty to err in lowering and granting rank; even if you executed us, it would not be enough to apologize to all under Heaven.

value.zh: 今大駕還宮，文武空曠，制度荒破，靡有孑遺，臣等雖劣，足匡王室。
value.en: Now the great carriage has returned to the palace, civil and military offices are empty, institutions are ruined and broken, and nothing remains. Although we your servants are inferior, we are enough to help correct the royal house.
value.literal: Now the great carriage has returned to the palace, civil and military offices are empty, institutions are ruined and broken, and nothing remains. Although we your servants are inferior, we are enough to help correct the royal house.

value.zh: 而道路之言，謂張方與臣等不同。
value.en: But talk on the roads says that Zhang Fang is not of one mind with us.
value.literal: But talk on the roads says that Zhang Fang is not of one mind with us.

value.zh: 既惜所在興異，又乙太宰惇德允元，著於具瞻，每當義節，輒為社稷宗盟之先。
value.en: We both regret that differences are arising where he is, and also because the Grand Steward is sincere in virtue and truly principal, visible to all who look up to him; whenever righteousness and integrity are at stake, he always stands first among the great allies of the altars of soil and grain.
value.literal: We both regret that differences are arising where he is, and also because the Grand Steward is sincere in virtue and truly principal, visible to all who look up to him; whenever righteousness and integrity are at stake, he always stands first among the great allies of the altars of soil and grain.

value.zh: 張方受其指教，為國效節。
value.en: Zhang Fang received his direction and instruction and showed integrity for the state.
value.literal: Zhang Fang received his direction and instruction and showed integrity for the state.

value.zh: 昔年之舉，有死無貳。
value.en: In last year's action, he had death before him and no second loyalty.
value.literal: In last year's action, he had death before him and no second loyalty.

value.zh: 此即太宰之良將，陛下之忠臣。
value.en: He is therefore a good general of the Grand Steward and a loyal subject of Your Majesty.
value.literal: He is therefore a good general of the Grand Steward and a loyal subject of Your Majesty.

value.zh: 但以受性強毅，不達變通，遂守前志，已致紛紜。
value.en: It is only because his nature is forceful and resolute and he does not understand adaptation that he kept to his former intention and has already caused confusion.
value.literal: It is only because his nature is forceful and resolute and he does not understand adaptation that he kept to his former intention and has already caused confusion.

value.zh: 然退思惟，既是其不易之節，且慮事翻之後，為天下所罪，故不即西還耳。
value.en: Yet when we withdraw and think on it, this is already his unchanging integrity, and he also worries that after affairs reverse, he will be blamed by all under Heaven; therefore he has not immediately returned west.
value.literal: Yet when we withdraw and think on it, this is already his unchanging integrity, and he also worries that after affairs reverse, he will be blamed by all under Heaven; therefore he has not immediately returned west.

value.zh: 原其本事，實無深責。
value.en: When the root of the matter is traced, there is in fact no deep blame.
value.literal: When the root of the matter is traced, there is in fact no deep blame.

value.zh: 臣聞先代明主，未嘗不全護功臣，令福流子孫。
value.en: We your servants have heard that enlightened rulers of earlier generations always preserved and protected meritorious ministers and made blessings flow to their descendants.
value.literal: We your servants have heard that enlightened rulers of earlier generations always preserved and protected meritorious ministers and made blessings flow to their descendants.

value.zh: 自中間以來，陛下功臣初無全者，非獨人才皆劣，其於取禍，實由朝廷策之失宜，不相容恕。
value.en: Since the recent troubled period, none of Your Majesty's meritorious ministers has been preserved. This is not only because the men were all inferior; their incurring disaster has truly come from the court's policies losing what was fitting and from failure to tolerate and forgive one another.
value.literal: Since the recent troubled period, none of Your Majesty's meritorious ministers has been preserved. This is not only because the men were all inferior; their incurring disaster has truly come from the court's policies losing what was fitting and from failure to tolerate and forgive one another.

value.zh: 以一旦之咎，喪其積年之勳，既違《周禮》議功之典，且使天下之人莫敢復為陛下致節者。
value.en: To lose accumulated years of merit because of one day's fault both violates the Zhouli canon of deliberating on merit and makes the people of the realm no longer dare to give their utmost loyalty for Your Majesty.
value.literal: To lose accumulated years of merit because of one day's fault both violates the Zhouli canon of deliberating on merit and makes the people of the realm no longer dare to give their utmost loyalty for Your Majesty.

value.zh: 臣等此言，豈獨為一張方，實為社稷遠計，欲令功臣長守富貴。
value.en: These words of ours are not only for one Zhang Fang; they are truly a long-range plan for the altars of soil and grain, wishing to let meritorious ministers long keep wealth and honor.
value.literal: These words of ours are not only for one Zhang Fang; they are truly a long-range plan for the altars of soil and grain, wishing to let meritorious ministers long keep wealth and honor.

value.zh: 臣愚以為宜委太宰以關右之任，一方事重，及自州郡已下，選舉授任，一皆仰成。
value.en: In our foolish view, it is fitting to entrust the Grand Steward with responsibility west of the passes. Affairs in that region are weighty, and from provinces and commanderies downward, selection, recommendation, appointment, and assignment should all look up to him for completion.
value.literal: In our foolish view, it is fitting to entrust the Grand Steward with responsibility west of the passes. Affairs in that region are weighty, and from provinces and commanderies downward, selection, recommendation, appointment, and assignment should all look up to him for completion.

value.zh: 若朝之大事，廢興損益，每輒疇諮。
value.en: As for great affairs of the court, abolitions, establishments, reductions, and additions, each should be consulted with him.
value.literal: As for great affairs of the court, abolitions, establishments, reductions, and additions, each should be consulted with him.

value.zh: 此則二伯述職，周召分陝之義，陛下復行於今時。
value.en: This would be Your Majesty carrying out again in the present age the meaning of the two regional chiefs reporting on their duties and of Zhou and Shao dividing Shaan.
value.literal: This would be Your Majesty carrying out again in the present age the meaning of the two regional chiefs reporting on their duties and of Zhou and Shao dividing Shaan.

value.zh: 遣方還郡，令群後申志，時定王室。
value.en: Send Fang back to his commandery, let the assembled nobles extend their intentions, and in time settle the royal house.
value.literal: Send Fang back to his commandery, let the assembled nobles extend their intentions, and in time settle the royal house.

value.zh: 所加方官，請悉如舊。
value.en: As for the offices added to Fang, we request that all be as before.
value.literal: As for the offices added to Fang, we request that all be as before.

value.zh: 此則忠臣義士有勸，功臣必全矣。
value.en: Then loyal ministers and righteous men will have encouragement, and meritorious ministers will surely be preserved.
value.literal: Then loyal ministers and righteous men will have encouragement, and meritorious ministers will surely be preserved.

value.zh: 司徒戎，異姓之賢；
value.en: Minister over the Masses Rong is a worthy of a different surname.
value.literal: Minister over the Masses Rong is a worthy of a different surname.

value.zh: 司空越，公族之望，並忠國愛主，小心翼翼，宜幹機事，委以朝政。
value.en: Minister of Works Yue is the hope of the imperial clan. Both are loyal to the state and love the ruler, careful and reverent, and should manage key affairs and be entrusted with court government.
value.literal: Minister of Works Yue is the hope of the imperial clan. Both are loyal to the state and love the ruler, careful and reverent, and should manage key affairs and be entrusted with court government.

value.zh: 安北將軍王浚佐命之胤，率身履道，忠亮清正，遠近所推。
value.en: General Who Pacifies the North Wang Jun is a descendant of one who assisted the mandate; he leads himself according to the Way, is loyal, bright, clear, and correct, and is recommended by those near and far.
value.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Wang Jun is a descendant of one who assisted the mandate; he leads himself according to the Way, is loyal, bright, clear, and correct, and is recommended by those near and far.

value.zh: 如今日之大舉，實有定社稷之勳，此是臣等所以歎息歸高也。
value.en: In a great undertaking like today's, he truly has merit in settling the altars of soil and grain; this is why we sigh in admiration and return high praise to him.
value.literal: In a great undertaking like today's, he truly has merit in settling the altars of soil and grain; this is why we sigh in admiration and return high praise to him.

value.zh: 浚宜特崇重之，以副群望，遂撫幽朔，長為北籓。
value.en: Jun should be specially exalted and honored in order to meet the hopes of the multitude, then pacify You and the northern lands and long serve as the northern shield.
value.literal: Jun should be specially exalted and honored in order to meet the hopes of the multitude, then pacify You and the northern lands and long serve as the northern shield.

value.zh: 臣等竭力扞城，籓屏皇家，陛下垂拱，而四海自正。
value.en: We your servants will exhaust our strength as defending walls and act as screens for the imperial house, while Your Majesty lets your robes hang and folds your hands, and the four seas will correct themselves.
value.literal: We your servants will exhaust our strength as defending walls and act as screens for the imperial house, while Your Majesty lets your robes hang and folds your hands, and the four seas will correct themselves.

value.zh: 則四祖之業，必隆於今，日月之暉，昧而復曜。
value.en: Then the enterprise of the Four Ancestors will surely flourish today, and the radiance of sun and moon, once dimmed, will shine again.
value.literal: Then the enterprise of the Four Ancestors will surely flourish today, and the radiance of sun and moon, once dimmed, will shine again.

value.zh: 乞垂三思，察臣所言。
value.en: We beg you to lower threefold thought and examine what we your servants have said.
value.literal: We beg you to lower threefold thought and examine what we your servants have said.

value.zh: 又可以臣表西示太宰。
value.en: You may also show our memorial westward to the Grand Steward.
value.literal: You may also show our memorial westward to the Grand Steward.

value.zh: 傅玄
value.en: Fu Xuan
value.literal: Fu Xuan.

value.zh: 時朝廷寬弛，豪右放恣，交私請托，朝野溷淆。
value.en: The court had grown lax; great families traded private favors until court and countryside were a blur.
value.literal: At that time the court was lax and slack; powerful magnates gave free rein, mingling private requests and entrustments; court and countryside were confused.

value.zh: 咸奏免河南尹澹、左將軍倩、廷尉高光、兼河南尹何攀等，京都肅然，貴戚懾伏。
value.en: Fu Xian impeached the governor of Henan (surnamed Dan), the general of the left (surnamed Qian), the commandant of justice Gao Guang, and the concurrent governor of Henan He Pan; the capital grew orderly and the great houses trembled.
value.literal: Xian memorialized to dismiss the governor of Henan, Dan, the general of the left, Qian, the commandant of justice Gao Guang, concurrent governor of Henan He Pan, and others; the capital was austere, and noble in-laws were awed into submission.

value.zh: 咸以「聖人久于其道，天下化成。
value.en: Fu Xian quoted: “When the sage long pursues his course, the realm is shaped by it.
value.literal: Xian cited: “When the sage is long on his way, all under Heaven is transformed and completed.

value.zh: 是以唐、虞三載考績，九年黜陟。
value.en: Thus under Tang and Yu officials were graded every three years and promoted or demoted over nine.
value.literal: Therefore Tang and Yu examined achievements over three years, promoting and demoting over nine years.

value.zh: 其在《周禮》，三年大比。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribes a great review every three years.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, there is the great comparison every three years.

value.zh: 孔子亦云，『三年有成』。
value.en: Confucius too said, “Give three years and there will be results.”
value.literal: Confucius also said, “In three years there is accomplishment.”

value.zh: 而中間以來，長吏到官，未幾便遷，百姓困于無定，吏卒疲於送迎」。
value.en: Yet of late magistrates are shuffled after a short stay; the people suffer endless instability, and runners collapse escorting one chief after another.”
value.literal: Yet in the middle period since then, when senior officers reach their post, before long they are transferred; the hundred surnames are worn out by having no stability, clerks and soldiers exhausted by seeing off and welcoming.”

value.zh: 時僕射王戎兼吏部，咸奏：「戎備位臺輔，兼掌選舉，不能謐靜風俗，以凝庶績，至令人心傾動，開張浮競。
value.en: Vice-director Wang Rong then ran the ministry of appointments; Fu Xian charged: “Rong sits among the chief ministers and holds appointments, yet he cannot steady custom or settle administration; hearts waver and empty rivalry spreads.
value.literal: At that time the vice-director Wang Rong concurrently held the ministry of appointments; Xian memorialized: “Rong occupies a place among ministerial supports and concurrently controls selection; he cannot calm custom and stillness, to coalesce the duties of the many—to the point of letting human hearts tilt and drift, opening and spreading empty rivalry.

value.zh: 中郎李重、李義不相匡正。
value.en: The gentleman-attendants Li Chong and Li Yi never correct him.
value.literal: The gentleman-attendants Li Chong and Li Yi do not correct him.

value.zh: 請免戎等官。」
value.en: I ask that Wang Rong and his like be removed from office.”
value.literal: I ask that Rong and others be dismissed from office.”

value.zh: 詔曰：「政道之本，誠宜久於其職，咸奏是也。
value.en: The edict said: “Long tenure is the root of good government; Fu Xian is right.
value.literal: The edict said: “The root of governing the way truly lies in long tenure in one’s post; what Xian memorialized is right.

value.zh: 戎職在論道，吾所崇委，其解禁止。」
value.en: Wang Rong’s duty is to counsel on the Way, which I value; lift the restrictions on him.”
value.literal: Rong’s duty lies in discussing the Way—I esteem and entrust him; as for him, dissolve the prohibition.”

value.zh: 御史中丞解結以咸劾戎為違典制，越局侵官，干非其分，奏免咸官。
value.en: Metropolitan censor Xie Jie argued that impeaching Wang Rong broke the rules, overstepped Fu Xian’s charge, and meddled beyond his rank; he asked that Fu Xian be dismissed.
value.literal: Metropolitan Censor Xie Jie held that Xian’s impeachment of Rong violated canonical regulation, overstepped his office and encroached on another’s duty, meddling beyond his portion, and memorialized to dismiss Xian from office.

value.zh: 詔亦不許。
value.en: The throne again refused.
value.literal: An edict again did not permit it.

value.zh: 楚王瑋之矯詔也，祗以聞奏稽留，免官。
value.en: When Prince Chu, Sima Wei, forged an edict, Fu Zhi was dismissed for slow reporting.
value.literal: When Prince Chu, Wei, forged the edict, Zhi because reporting was delayed was dismissed.

value.zh: 期年，遷光祿勳，復以公事免。
value.en: A year later he became grand master of splendid horses, then was removed again over a public affair.
value.literal: After a full year he was promoted grand master of splendid horses; again for public affairs he was dismissed.

value.zh: 氐人齊萬年舉兵反，以祗為行安西軍司，加常侍，率安西將軍夏侯駿討平之。
value.en: When the Di leader Qi Wannian rebelled, Fu Zhi served as acting chief of staff for the Army of the West with concurrent regular attendant, accompanying General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to crush the revolt.
value.literal: The Di man Qi Wannian raised troops in revolt; Zhi was made acting army director of Pacifying-the-West, with concurrent regular attendant, and led General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to strike and pacify him.

value.zh: 遷衛尉，以風疾遜位，就拜常侍，食卿祿秩，賜錢及床帳等。
value.en: Promoted commandant of the guards, he resigned with a palsy, was kept as regular attendant on ministerial salary, and given cash, bedding, and the like.
value.literal: He was promoted commandant of the guards, on wind illness yielded place, was then appointed regular attendant, ate ministerial salary ranks, was granted cash, bed-curtains, and so on.

value.zh: 尋加光祿大夫，門施行馬。
value.en: Soon he added the title grand counsellor of splendid horses and was allowed the mounted patrol barrier at his gate.
value.literal: Soon he was added grand counsellor of splendid horses; mounted patrol lanes were set up at his gate.

value.zh: 及趙王倫輔政，以為中書監，常侍如故，以鎮眾心。
value.en: When Prince Zhao, Sima Lun, took charge, he made Fu Zhi overseer of the secretariat, still a regular attendant, to calm public opinion.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao, Lun, directed the government, he made him overseer of the secretariat, regular attendant as before, to steady the host of hearts.

value.zh: 祗辭之以疾，倫遣御史輿祗就職。
value.en: Fu Zhi pleaded illness; Lun sent a censor with a litter to force him to his desk.
value.literal: Zhi declined on grounds of illness; Lun sent a censor to carry Zhi in a litter to take up office.

value.zh: 王戎、陳准等相與言曰：「傅公在事，吾屬無憂矣。」
value.en: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun said to each other, ‘With Lord Fu at the helm we need not worry.’
value.literal: Wang Rong, Chen Zhun, and others spoke together: "With Lord Fu in charge, our sort has no worries."

value.zh: 其為物所倚信如此。
value.en: Such was the trust men placed in him.
value.literal: Thus he was trusted by others to this degree.

value.zh: 郤詵
value.en: Xi Shen.
value.literal: Xi Shen.

value.zh: 永甯初，出為郟令。
value.en: In Yongning he became magistrate of Jia.
value.literal: At the beginning of Yongning—went out as magistrate of Jia.

value.zh: 于時兵亂之後，境內饑饉，譚傾心撫䘏。
value.en: After war famine stalked his district—Tan poured himself into relief.
value.literal: At that time after military chaos—within the borders famine—Tan poured heart into comforting relief.

value.zh: 司徒王戎聞而善之，出穀三百斛以助之。
value.en: Wang Rong heard and sent three hundred hu of grain.
value.literal: Minister Wang Rong hearing praised him—issued grain three hundred hu to assist.

value.zh: 譚甚有政績，再遷廬江內史，加綏遠將軍。
value.en: His rule excelled—he rose to interior governor of Lujiang with the Pacify-the-Distant generalship.
value.literal: Tan had very good administrative merit—promoted again to Interior Governor of Lujiang—added General Who Pacifies the Distance.

value.zh: 時石冰之党陸圭等屯據諸縣，譚遣司馬褚敦討平之。
value.en: When Lu Gui's band held counties for Shi Bing, Tan sent Chu Dun to crush them.
value.literal: At that time Shi Bing's faction Lu Gui and others garrisoned and held various counties—Tan dispatched Marshal Chu Dun to punish and pacify.

value.zh: 又遣別軍擊冰都督孟徐，獲其驍率。
value.en: Another column struck Meng Xu—taking his fiercest captain.
value.literal: He also dispatched separate troops to strike Bing's commander-in-chief Meng Xu—captured his fierce leader.

value.zh: 以功封都亭侯，食邑千戶，賜絹千匹。
value.en: For merit he became Village Marquis—thousand-house fief and thousand bolts of silk.
value.literal: By merit ennobled Village Marquis—food estate thousand households—silk thousand bolts.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 紹始入洛，或謂王戎曰：「昨于稠人中始見嵇紹，昂昂然如野鶴之在雞群。」
value.en: When Shao first arrived in Luoyang, someone remarked to Wang Rong: "Yesterday, in the press of people, I saw Ji Shao for the first time—stately as a crane among barnyard fowl."
value.literal: When Shao first entered Luoyang, someone said to Wang Rong: "Yesterday amid the crowd I first saw Ji Shao—towering, like a wild crane among chickens."

value.zh: 戎曰：「君復未見其父耳。」
value.en: Wang Rong answered: "Then you have not met his father."
value.literal: Rong said: "You have still not seen his father."

value.zh: 累遷汝陰太守。
value.en: He rose through successive posts to Administrator of Ruyin.
value.literal: He was promoted in stages to Administrator of Ruyin.

value.zh: 尚書左僕射裴頠亦深器之，每曰：「使延祖為吏部尚書，可使天下無復遺才矣。」
value.en: Pei Yi, Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat, thought the world of him and used to say: "Put Yanzu in charge of personnel and no able man in the empire would go unused."
value.literal: Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat Pei Yi also deeply esteemed him, often saying: "Were Yanzu made Minister of Personnel, he could make it so the realm had no overlooked talent again."

value.zh: 沛國戴晞少有才智，與紹從子含相友善，時人許以遠致，紹以為必不成器。
value.en: Dai Xi of Pei was clever as a youth and close to Shao's nephew Ji Han; contemporaries predicted a brilliant career, yet Shao insisted he would never amount to anything.
value.literal: Dai Xi of Pei was clever from youth and friendly with Shao's nephew Ji Han; people of the time promised him far-reaching success, but Shao believed he would surely fail to become a useful vessel.

value.zh: 晞後為司州主簿，以無行被斥，州黨稱紹有知人之明。
value.en: Xi later served as Si Province registrar until dismissed for scandalous behavior; locals then credited Shao with sound judgment of character.
value.literal: Xi later became Registrar of Si Province and was dismissed for misconduct; his provincial circle praised Shao's discernment of men.

value.zh: 轉豫章內史，以母憂，不之官。
value.en: He was named Interior Governor of Yuzhang but stayed home to mourn his mother and never took up the post.
value.literal: He was transferred to Interior Governor of Yuzhang but, owing to mourning for his mother, did not take up the post.

value.zh: 服闋，拜徐州刺史。
value.en: When mourning ended, he received appointment as Governor of Xuzhou.
value.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed Governor of Xuzhou.

value.zh: 時石崇為都督，性雖驕暴，而紹將之以道，崇甚親敬之。
value.en: Shi Chong was regional commander then—arrogant and harsh by nature—but Shao guided him with moral authority, and Chong came to trust and respect him deeply.
value.literal: At the time Shi Chong was area commander; though by nature arrogant and violent, Shao led him by principle, and Chong greatly favored and respected him.

value.zh: 後以長子喪去職。
value.en: He later resigned when his eldest son died.
value.literal: Later he left office upon the death of his eldest son.

value.zh: 荀彧字文若，潁川潁陰人也。
value.en: Xun Yu, courtesy name Wenruo, came from Yingyin in Yingchuan.
value.literal: Xun Yu, styled Wenruo, was a man of Yingyin in Yingchuan commandery.

value.zh: 祖父淑，字季和，朗陵令。
value.en: His grandfather Shu, courtesy name Jihe, had served as magistrate of Langling.
value.literal: His grandfather Shu, styled Jihe, was magistrate of Langling.

value.zh: 當漢順、桓之間，知名當世。
value.en: Under Emperors Shun and Huan of Han he was already famous in his own day.
value.literal: During the reigns of Shun and Huan of Han, he was known by name in the age.

value.zh: 有子八人，號曰八龍。
value.en: He fathered eight sons, who were known collectively as the Eight Dragons.
value.literal: He had eight sons, called the Eight Dragons.

value.zh: 彧父緄，濟南相。
value.en: Xun Yu’s father, Gun, had been chancellor of the kingdom of Jinan.
value.literal: Yu’s father Gun was chancellor of Jinan kingdom.

value.zh: 叔父爽，司空。
value.en: His uncle Shuang rose to be Minister of Works.
value.literal: His uncle Shuang was Minister of Works.

value.zh: 十七年，董昭等謂太祖宜進爵國公，九錫備物，以彰殊勳，密以諮彧。
value.en: In the seventeenth year, Dong Zhao and others urged that the Grand Progenitor be raised to Duke of a State with the full nine bestowals to honor his exceptional achievements, and they quietly sought Yu's counsel.
value.literal: In the seventeenth year, Dong Zhao and others said the Grand Progenitor should be advanced to the rank of Duke of a State, with the nine bestowals and all their appurtenances, to manifest extraordinary merit, and secretly consulted Yu about it.

value.zh: 彧以爲太祖本興義兵以匡朝寧國，秉忠貞之誠，守退讓之實；
value.en: Yu held that the Grand Progenitor had originally raised righteous armies to restore the dynasty and pacify the realm, maintaining loyal integrity and the virtue of modest restraint;
value.literal: Yu believed that the Grand Progenitor had originally raised righteous troops to rectify the court and pacify the state, holding to the sincerity of loyalty and steadfastness, and keeping to the reality of yielding and modesty;

value.zh: 君子愛人以德，不宜如此。
value.en: A gentleman shows care for others through virtue — such a course was inappropriate.
value.literal: A gentleman loves others through virtue; it is not fitting to act thus.

value.zh: 太祖由是心不能平。
value.en: The Grand Progenitor consequently took this badly at heart.
value.literal: Because of this, the Grand Progenitor's heart could not be at ease.

value.zh: 會征孫權，表請彧勞軍于譙，因輒留彧，以侍中光祿大夫持節，參丞相軍事。
value.en: When Cao Cao marched against Sun Quan, he petitioned to have Yu encourage the troops at Qiao, then kept him there — appointing him Palace Attendant and Household Counsellor with credentials of authority to assist the Chancellor in military affairs.
value.literal: It happened that when campaigning against Sun Quan, he memorialized requesting that Yu encourage the troops at Qiao, and on this pretext detained Yu, appointing him Palace Attendant and Household Counsellor bearing credentials of authority, to participate in military affairs of the Chancellor.

value.zh: 太祖軍至濡須，彧疾留壽春，以憂薨，時年五十。
value.en: When the Grand Progenitor's army reached Ruxu, Yu fell ill and remained at Shouchun, where he died of grief at the age of fifty.
value.literal: When the Grand Progenitor's army reached Ruxu, Yu fell ill and remained at Shouchun; he died of grief, aged fifty at the time.

value.zh: 諡曰敬侯。
value.en: He was posthumously titled Marquis Jing.
value.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Jing.

value.zh: 明年，太祖遂爲魏公矣。
value.en: The following year, the Grand Progenitor became Duke of Wei.
value.literal: The next year, the Grand Progenitor then became Duke of Wei.

value.zh: 《魏氏春秋》曰：太祖饋彧食，發之乃空器也，於是飲藥而卒。
value.en: The Wei Clan Annals says that the Grand Progenitor sent Yu food, but when he opened it, the container was empty — whereupon Yu drank poison and died.
value.literal: The Wei Clan Annals states: The Grand Progenitor sent Yu food; when he opened it, it was an empty vessel; whereupon he drank medicine and died.

value.zh: 咸熙二年，贈彧太尉。
value.en: In the second year of Xianxi, Yu was posthumously awarded the rank of Grand Commandant.
value.literal: In the second year of Xianxi, Yu was posthumously granted the office of Grand Commandant.

value.zh: 《彧別傳》曰：彧自爲尚書令，常以書陳事，臨薨，皆焚毀之，故奇策密謀不得盡聞也。
value.en: The Separate Biography of Yu records that from his time as Director of the Masters of Writing, he habitually submitted affairs in writing; on his deathbed he burned them all, so his most ingenious strategies were never fully known.
value.literal: The Separate Biography of Yu states: From the time Yu served as Director of the Masters of Writing, he often submitted affairs in written memorials; on the verge of death, he burned and destroyed them all; therefore extraordinary plans and secret stratagems could not be fully heard of.

value.zh: 是時征役草創，制度多所興復，彧嘗言於太祖曰：「昔舜分命禹、稷、契、皐陶以揆庶績，教化征伐，並時而用。
value.en: At that time campaigns and corvée were still being organized and many institutions were being revived. Yu once told the Grand Progenitor: "Long ago, Shun separately charged Yu, Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao with governing the people's affairs — civilizing instruction and military campaigns were pursued at the same time.
value.literal: At that time military campaigns and corvée labor were in their initial stages, and institutions were being widely revived; Yu once said to the Grand Progenitor: "In ancient times Shun separately appointed Yu, Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao to oversee the multitude of achievements; civilizing instruction and military expeditions were employed simultaneously.

value.zh: 及髙祖之初，金革方殷，猶舉民能善教訓者，叔孫通習禮儀於戎旅之閒，世祖有投戈講藝、息馬論道之事，君子無終食之閒違仁。
value.en: Even at the beginning of the Han, when warfare was still fierce, the court still sought out men capable of teaching and instruction — Shusun Tong mastered ritual amid military encampments, and Emperor Guangwu set aside arms to lecture on the classics and rested horses to discuss the Way. A gentleman does not neglect benevolence even for the span of a single meal.
value.literal: At the beginning of the High Ancestor's reign, the clash of arms and armor was still intense, yet he still elevated those among the people able to teach and instruct well; Shusun Tong became versed in ritual propriety amid military camps; the World Ancestor had occasions for casting aside weapons to lecture on the arts and resting horses to discuss the Way; a gentleman has not even the interval of a single meal in which to depart from benevolence.

value.zh: 今公外定武功，内興文學，使干戈戢睦，大道流行，國難方弭，六禮倶治，此姬旦宰周之所以速平也。
value.en: Now you have subdued the realm by force abroad and are fostering scholarship at home — weapons are being laid aside, the Great Way spreads, national crisis is being resolved, and the six rites are being restored. This is how the Duke of Zhou governed Zhou and brought peace so swiftly.
value.literal: Now my lord outwardly settles martial achievements and inwardly raises literary studies, causing weapons and armor to be laid aside in peace, the Great Way to spread, national troubles just to be quelled, and the six rites all to be governed — this is why the Duke of Zhou governed Zhou and brought rapid peace.

value.zh: 旣立德立功，而又兼立言，成仲尼述作之意；
value.en: You have established virtue and merit, and by adding literary achievement you fulfill Confucius's purpose in his writings;
value.literal: Having already established virtue and established merit, and furthermore also establishing words, fulfilling the intent of Zhongni's compositions;

value.zh: 顯制度於當時，揚名於後世，豈不盛哉！
value.en: making your institutions manifest in your own age and your fame endure for posterity — what could be more splendid!
value.literal: displaying institutions in the present age, spreading one's fame in later generations — how could it not be magnificent!

value.zh: 若須武事畢而後制作，以稽治化，於事未敏。
value.en: If you wait until all military matters are finished before turning to cultural institutions in order to examine governance and transformation, you will have been too slow.
value.literal: If one must wait until military affairs are concluded before then undertaking cultural creation, in order to examine governance and transformation, in affairs this lacks keenness.

value.zh: 宜集天下大才通儒，考論六經，刊定傳記，存古今之學，除其煩重，以一聖眞，並隆禮學，漸敦教化，則王道兩濟。」
value.en: You should assemble the empire's greatest scholars and Confucian experts to examine and discuss the Six Classics, standardize the commentarial traditions, preserve learning ancient and modern while eliminating what is redundant, unify them around the sage's true teaching, and together elevate ritual learning to gradually deepen civilizing instruction — then the royal Way will be fully realized on both fronts."
value.literal: It would be fitting to gather the great talents and thoroughly learned Confucians of the empire, examine and discuss the Six Classics, edit and fix the commentarial traditions, preserve the learning of past and present, remove what is cumbersome and redundant, unite them in the one true teaching of the sage, and together elevate the study of ritual, gradually thickening civilizing instruction — then the royal Way would be served on both sides."

value.zh: 彧從容與太祖論治道，如此之類甚衆，太祖常嘉納之。
value.en: Yu often discussed principles of governance with the Grand Progenitor in an unhurried manner; the Grand Progenitor frequently approved and adopted his counsel.
value.literal: Yu calmly discussed principles of governance with the Grand Progenitor; matters of this sort were very numerous; the Grand Progenitor often commended and accepted them.

value.zh: 彧德行周備，非正道不用心，名重天下，莫不以爲儀表，海内英儁咸宗焉。
value.en: Yu's virtue and conduct were complete in every respect; he devoted himself only to the right path. His fame resounded throughout the realm, and all regarded him as a model — the most distinguished men in the land looked up to him.
value.literal: Yu's virtue and conduct were comprehensive and complete; he would not apply his mind except to the correct Way; his renown weighed heavily throughout the realm; none did not regard him as a model; eminent talents within the seas all looked up to him.

value.zh: 司馬宣王常稱書傳遠事，吾自耳目所從聞見，逮百數十年間，賢才未有及荀令君者也。
value.en: The Lord of Xuan (Sima Yi) often said: "In historical records and in what I myself have witnessed over more than a hundred years, I have seen no talent to equal Director Xun."
value.literal: The Lord of Xuan, Sima Yi, often said: "In what is recorded in books and transmitted from distant events, and in what I myself have heard and seen from my own eyes and ears, spanning a hundred and some decades, there has been no talented man who could match Director Xun."

value.zh: 前後所舉者，命世大才，邦邑則荀攸、鍾繇、陳羣，海内則司馬宣王，及引致當世知名郗慮、華歆、王朗、荀恱、杜襲、辛毗、趙儼之儔，終爲卿相，以十數人。
value.en: Those he recommended over the years were truly exceptional talents: Xun You, Zhong Yao, and Chen Qun from his home region; the Lord of Xuan from across the realm; and he also recruited such celebrated figures as Xi Lu, Hua Xin, Wang Lang, Xun Yue, Du Xi, Xin Pi, and Zhao Yan — more than a dozen in all who rose to ministerial rank.
value.literal: Those he recommended before and after were world-shaking great talents: within his native region, Xun You, Zhong Yao, and Chen Qun; within the seas, the Lord of Xuan; and he also brought in the well-known men of the age, Xi Lu, Hua Xin, Wang Lang, Xun Yue, Du Xi, Xin Pi, Zhao Yan, and the like — who in the end became ministers and chancellors, numbering more than a dozen.

value.zh: 取士不以一揆，戲志才、郭嘉等有負俗之譏，杜畿簡傲少文，皆以智策舉之，終各顯名。
value.en: He did not select men by a single standard: Xi Zhicai and Guo Jia had reputations for violating convention, and Du Ji was austere, proud, and unpolished — yet he recommended all of them for their strategic brilliance, and each rose to prominence.
value.literal: In selecting scholars he did not use a single standard; Xi Zhicai and Guo Jia and others bore criticisms for violating custom; Du Ji was frugal, proud, and lacking in refinement — all were recommended through their strategic intelligence, and in the end each achieved distinguished fame.

value.zh: 荀攸後爲魏尚書令，亦推賢進士。
value.en: Xun You later served as Wei Director of the Masters of Writing and likewise promoted worthy talents.
value.literal: Xun You later served as Director of the Masters of Writing for Wei and also promoted worthy men and advanced scholars.

value.zh: 太祖曰：「二荀令之論人，久而益信，吾沒世不忘。」
value.en: The Grand Progenitor said: "The two Directors Xun judged men so well that time only confirms their judgment — I shall never forget it."
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "The two Directors Xun's judgments of men, the longer they stand the more trustworthy they prove — I shall not forget them while I live."

value.zh: 鍾繇以爲顏子旣沒，能備九德，不貳其過，唯荀彧然。
value.en: Zhong Yao believed that since Yan Hui's death, only Xun Yu had possessed all nine virtues without wavering from his principles.
value.literal: Zhong Yao held that since Yanzi died, only Xun Yu could possess all nine virtues and not stray from his errors.

value.zh: 或問繇曰：「君雅重荀君，比之顏子，自以不及，可得聞乎？」
value.en: Someone asked Zhong Yao: "You greatly esteem Lord Xun and compare him to Yan Hui, yet say you cannot match him — may we hear why?"
value.literal: Someone asked Yao: "You greatly esteem Lord Xun, comparing him to Yanzi, yet consider yourself unequal — may we hear your reasons?"

value.zh: 曰：「夫明君師臣，其次友之。
value.en: He replied: "An enlightened lord treats his minister as a teacher, or at least as a friend.
value.literal: He said: "An enlightened lord treats his minister as a teacher, or at least as a friend.

value.zh: 以太祖之聦明，毎有大事，常先諮之荀君，是則古師友之義也。
value.en: Given the Grand Progenitor's brilliance, whenever a major matter arose he always consulted Lord Xun first — that is the ancient ideal of a teacher-friend relationship.
value.literal: With the Grand Progenitor's brilliance, whenever there was a major affair, he would always first consult Lord Xun — this is the ancient meaning of teacher and friend.

value.zh: 吾等受命而行，猶或不盡，相去顧不遠邪！」
value.en: We merely receive orders and carry them out, and even then we sometimes fall short — are we not rather close to each other in standing!"
value.literal: We receive orders and carry them out, yet still sometimes fall short — the distance between us, does it not seem not far!"

value.zh: 《獻帝春秋》曰：董承之誅，伏后與父完書，言司空殺董承，帝方爲報怨。
value.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Emperor Xian records that after Dong Cheng's execution, Empress Fu wrote to her father Fu Wan, saying the Minister of Works had killed Dong Cheng and the Emperor was now bent on revenge.
value.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Emperor Xian states: After Dong Cheng's execution, Empress Fu wrote to her father Wan, saying the Minister of Works had killed Dong Cheng and the Emperor was now seeking revenge.

value.zh: 完得書以示彧，彧惡之，久隱而不言。
value.en: Fu Wan received the letter and showed it to Yu; Yu was appalled but kept silent about it for a long time.
value.literal: Wan received the letter and showed it to Yu; Yu hated it and for a long time concealed it without speaking.

value.zh: 完以示妻弟樊普，普封以呈太祖，太祖陰爲之備。
value.en: Fu Wan showed it to his wife's younger brother Fan Pu, who sealed it and presented it to the Grand Progenitor; Cao Cao secretly began to prepare against the threat.
value.literal: Wan showed it to his wife's younger brother Fan Pu; Pu sealed it and presented it to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor secretly made preparations on account of it.

value.zh: 彧後恐事覺，欲自發之，因求使至鄴，勸太祖以女配帝。
value.en: Yu later feared discovery and wished to expose the matter himself; he requested permission to go to Ye as envoy and urged the Grand Progenitor to marry his daughter to the Emperor.
value.literal: Yu later feared the matter would be discovered and wished to expose it himself; he therefore requested to be sent as envoy to Ye, and urged the Grand Progenitor to marry his daughter to the Emperor.

value.zh: 太祖曰：「今朝廷有伏后，吾女何得以配上，吾以微功見録，位爲宰相，豈復賴女寵乎！」
value.en: The Grand Progenitor said: "The court already has Empress Fu — how can my daughter be made empress? I rose to the chancellorship on modest merit alone — must I rely on my daughter's favor now?"
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Now the court has Empress Fu — how could my daughter be matched to ascend the throne? I was recorded for minor achievements and occupy the post of chancellor — would I still depend on my daughter's favor!"

value.zh: 彧曰：「伏后無子，性又凶邪，往常與父書，言辭醜惡，可因此廢也。」
value.en: Yu said: "Empress Fu has no children, and her nature is vicious and depraved. Her letters to her father were full of ugly and vile language — she can be deposed on that basis."
value.literal: Yu said: "Empress Fu has no son, and her nature is also fierce and wicked; she often wrote to her father with ugly and vile language — she can be deposed on this account."

value.zh: 太祖曰：「卿昔何不道之？」
value.en: The Grand Progenitor said: "Why didn't you tell me this before?"
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Why did you not speak of this before?"

value.zh: 彧陽驚曰：「昔已嘗爲公言也。」
value.en: Yu feigned surprise and said: "I already told you about it long ago."
value.literal: Yu feigned surprise and said: "In the past I had already spoken to you about it."

value.zh: 太祖曰：「此豈小事而吾忘之！」
value.en: The Grand Progenitor said: "This is hardly a trifling matter — how could I have forgotten it!"
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "How could this be a minor matter and I have forgotten it!"

value.zh: 彧又驚曰：「誠未語公邪！
value.en: Yu feigned surprise again: "Truly I never told you, my lord!
value.literal: Yu was surprised again and said: "Truly I did not tell you, my lord!

value.zh: 昔公在官渡與袁紹相持，恐增内顧之念，故不言爾。」
value.en: When you were at Guandu in stalemate with Yuan Shao, I feared it would distract you with domestic worries, so I said nothing."
value.literal: In the past when you were at Guandu locked in stalemate with Yuan Shao, I feared increasing thoughts of looking back within — therefore I did not speak of it."

value.zh: 太祖曰：「官渡事後何以不言？」
value.en: The Grand Progenitor said: "Why didn't you speak after Guandu?"
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "After the affair at Guandu, why did you not speak?"

value.zh: 彧無對，謝闕而已。
value.en: Yu had no answer and could only apologize for his failure.
value.literal: Yu had no reply; he merely apologized for his lapse.

value.zh: 太祖以此恨彧，而外含容之，故世莫得知。
value.en: The Grand Progenitor harbored resentment over this but concealed it outwardly, so the world never knew.
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor on this account bore resentment toward Yu, yet outwardly tolerated him; therefore the world did not know of it.

value.zh: 至董昭建立魏公之議，彧意不同，欲言之於太祖。
value.en: When Dong Zhao proposed establishing the Duke of Wei, Yu disagreed and wished to speak to the Grand Progenitor about it.
value.literal: When it came to Dong Zhao's proposal to establish the Grand Progenitor as Duke of Wei, Yu's view differed; he wished to speak of it to the Grand Progenitor.

value.zh: 及齎璽書犒軍，飲饗禮畢，彧留請閒。
value.en: When Yu arrived bearing the imperial edict to reward the troops and the banquet concluded, he stayed behind to request a private audience.
value.literal: When he brought the imperial edict written on jade to reward the troops and the banquet rites were concluded, Yu remained to request a private audience.

value.zh: 太祖知彧欲言封事，揖而遣之，彧遂不得言。
value.en: The Grand Progenitor knew Yu wanted to discuss the enfeoffment; he bowed and dismissed him, and Yu never got to speak.
value.literal: The Grand Progenitor knew Yu wished to speak about the enfeoffment matter; he bowed and dismissed him; Yu thus could not speak.

value.zh: 彧卒於壽春，壽春亡者告孫權，言太祖使彧殺伏后，彧不從，故自殺。
value.en: When Yu died at Shouchun, a refugee from that city told Sun Quan that the Grand Progenitor had ordered Yu to kill Empress Fu, that Yu refused, and therefore killed himself.
value.literal: Yu died at Shouchun; a refugee from Shouchun informed Sun Quan, saying the Grand Progenitor had ordered Yu to kill Empress Fu and Yu refused, therefore killing himself.

value.zh: 權以露布於蜀，劉備聞之，曰：「老賊不死，禍亂未已。」
value.en: Sun Quan publicized this account to Shu; when Liu Bei heard it, he said: "That old villain is not dead — the turmoil is far from over."
value.literal: Sun Quan broadcast this by open proclamation to Shu; when Liu Bei heard it, he said: "The old villain does not die — calamity and disorder are not yet ended."

value.zh: 臣松之案《獻帝春秋》云彧欲發伏后事而求使至鄴，而方誣太祖云「昔已嘗言」。
value.en: Pei Songzhi notes: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Emperor Xian says Yu wished to expose the Empress Fu affair and sought an envoy mission to Ye, yet then falsely told the Grand Progenitor "I had already told you."
value.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Emperor Xian says that Yu wished to expose the Empress Fu matter and therefore requested to be sent to Ye, yet then falsely accused the Grand Progenitor, saying "I had already spoken before."

value.zh: 言旣無徴，迴託以官渡之虞，俛仰之間，辭情頓屈，雖在庸人，猶不至此，何以玷累賢哲哉！
value.en: His claim had no basis; he then pivoted to the excuse of Guandu — and in that exchange his argument collapsed utterly. Even an ordinary man would not behave so — how could such conduct be imputed to a worthy sage!
value.literal: The words had no evidence; he then turned and excused himself with the worry at Guandu; in the lowering and raising of his head, his words and feelings suddenly collapsed — even among ordinary men, it would not reach this point; how could it stain and burden a worthy sage!

value.zh: 凡諸云云，皆出自鄙俚，可謂以吾儕之言而厚誣君子者矣。
value.en: All such accounts come from vulgar sources — they use the words of common folk to slander a gentleman most unjustly.
value.literal: All such talk in every case originates from vulgar folk; it may be said to use words of people like us to falsely and heavily accuse a gentleman.

value.zh: 袁暐虚罔之類，此最爲甚也。
value.en: Among fabricators like Yuan Hui, this case is the worst.
value.literal: Among the false and groundless sorts like Yuan Hui, this is the most extreme.

value.zh: 子惲，嗣侯，官至虎賁中郎將。
value.en: His son Yun succeeded to the marquisate and rose to Tiger Guard Commander of the Central.
value.literal: His son Yun succeeded to the marquisate and reached the office of Tiger Guard Commander of the Central.

value.zh: 初，文帝與平原侯植並有擬論，文帝曲禮事彧。
value.en: Early on, both Emperor Wen and the Marquis of Pingyuan (Cao Zhi) were contenders for succession; Emperor Wen treated Yu with especial courtesy.
value.literal: Initially, Emperor Wen and the Marquis of Pingyuan Zhi both had aspirations to succession; Emperor Wen bent to courtesy in serving Yu.

value.zh: 及彧卒，惲又與植善，而與夏侯尚不穆，文帝深恨惲。
