value.en: After Yu's death, Yun remained friendly with Cao Zhi but was on bad terms with Xiahou Shang; Emperor Wen deeply resented him.
value.literal: When Yu died, Yun was again on good terms with Zhi, yet was not harmonious with Xiahou Shang; Emperor Wen deeply resented Yun.

value.zh: 惲早卒，子甝、霬，音翼。
value.en: Yun died young, leaving sons Kan and Hui (the latter pronounced Yi).
value.literal: Yun died young; his sons Kan and Hui — Hui is pronounced Yi.

value.zh: 以外甥故猶寵待。
value.en: Because of the family connection by marriage, they were still treated with favor.
value.literal: Because of the connection as nephew by marriage, he was still treated with favor.

value.zh: 惲弟俁，御史中丞，俁弟詵，大將軍從事中郎，皆知名，早卒。
value.en: Yun's younger brother Hou served as Censor-in-Chief; Hou's younger brother Shen served as Staff Officer to the General-in-Chief — all were well known and died young.
value.literal: Yun's younger brother Hou was Censor-in-Chief; Hou's younger brother Shen was Staff Officer to the General-in-Chief — all were well known and died young.

value.zh: 《荀氏家傳》曰：惲字長倩，俁字叔倩，詵字曼倩，俁子寓，字景伯。
value.en: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan records: Yun styled Changqian, Hou styled Shuqian, Shen styled Manqian, and Hou's son Yu styled Jingbo.
value.literal: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan states: Yun's style name was Changqian, Hou's was Shuqian, Shen's was Manqian, and Hou's son Yu's style name was Jingbo.

value.zh: 《世語》曰：寓少與裴楷、王戎、杜默倶有名京邑，仕晉，位至尚書，名見顯著。
value.en: The Tales of the Age records that in youth Yu was as famous in the capital as Pei Kai, Wang Rong, and Du Mo; serving Jin, he rose to Master of Writing with great renown.
value.literal: The Tales of the Age states: Yu in his youth was together with Pei Kai, Wang Rong, and Du Mo equally famous in the capital; he served Jin and reached the office of Master of Writing; his fame was conspicuous.

value.zh: 子羽嗣，位至尚書。
value.en: His son Yu succeeded him and rose to Master of Writing.
value.literal: His son Yu succeeded and reached the office of Master of Writing.

value.zh: 詵弟顗，咸熙中爲司空。
value.en: Shen's younger brother Yi served as Minister of Works during the Xianxi period.
value.literal: Shen's younger brother Yi, in the Xianxi period served as Minister of Works.

value.zh: 《晉陽秋》曰：顗字景倩，幼爲姊夫陳羣所異。
value.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Jin records that Yi styled Jingqian and was recognized as extraordinary in youth by his brother-in-law Chen Qun.
value.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Jin states: Yi's style name was Jingqian; in youth he was regarded as extraordinary by his sister's husband Chen Qun.

value.zh: 博學洽聞，意思愼密。
value.en: He was erudite and well informed, with careful and penetrating judgment.
value.literal: He was broadly learned and well informed; his thoughts were careful and close.

value.zh: 司馬宣王見顗，奇之，曰：「荀令君之子也。
value.en: When the Lord of Xuan (Sima Yi) met Yi, he was struck by him and said: "He is Director Xun's son.
value.literal: The Lord of Xuan saw Yi and marveled at him, saying: "This is the son of Director Xun.

value.zh: 近見袁偘，亦曜卿之子也。」
value.en: I recently met Yuan Kan — he too is Lord Yao's son."
value.literal: Recently I saw Yuan Kan — he too is the son of Lord Yao."

value.zh: 擢拜散騎侍郎。
value.en: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.
value.literal: He was promoted and appointed Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.

value.zh: 顗佐命晉室，位至太尉，封臨淮康公。
value.en: Yi assisted in establishing the Jin dynasty, rose to Grand Commandant, and was enfeoffed as Duke Kang of Linhuai.
value.literal: Yi assisted in founding the Jin house, reached the office of Grand Commandant, and was enfeoffed as Duke Kang of Linhuai.

value.zh: 嘗難鍾會「易無互體」，見稱於世。
value.en: He once disputed Zhong Hui's claim that "the Book of Changes has no mutual imagery," earning renown throughout the realm.
value.literal: He once challenged Zhong Hui's proposition that "there is no mutual imagery in the Changes," and was praised by the world.

value.zh: 顗弟粲，字奉倩。
value.en: Yi's younger brother Can styled Fengqian.
value.literal: Yi's younger brother Can's style name was Fengqian.

value.zh: 何劭爲粲傳曰：粲字奉倩，粲諸兄並以儒術論議，而粲獨好言道，常以爲子貢稱夫子之言性與天道，不可得聞，然則六籍雖存，固聖人之糠粃。
value.en: He Shao wrote a biography of Can: Can styled Fengqian. His elder brothers all debated in the Confucian tradition, but Can alone loved to discuss the Way. He often argued that since Zigong said the Master's words on human nature and the Way of Heaven could not be fully conveyed, the Six Classics, though preserved, are but the sage's chaff.
value.literal: He Shao wrote a biography of Can stating: Can's style name was Fengqian; Can's elder brothers all engaged in Confucian learning and debate, but Can alone delighted in discussing the Way; he often held that when Zigong said the Master's words on human nature and the Way of Heaven could not be heard, then although the Six Classics remained, they were truly the chaff of the sage.

value.zh: 粲兄俁難曰：「易亦云聖人立象以盡意，繫辭焉以盡言，則微言胡爲不可得而聞見哉？」
value.en: Can's elder brother Hou objected: "The Book of Changes says the sage established images to fully express meaning and appended words to fully express speech — then why could subtle teachings not be heard?"
value.literal: Can's elder brother Hou challenged him, saying: "The Changes also says the sage established images to fully express meaning and attached words to fully express speech — then why could subtle words not be obtained and heard and seen?"

value.zh: 粲荅曰：「蓋理之微者，非物象之所舉也。
value.en: Can replied: "Subtle principles cannot be fully conveyed through material images.
value.literal: Can replied: "Principles that are subtle are not what material images can fully express.

value.zh: 今稱立象以盡意，此非通于意外者也。
value.en: To say that establishing images fully expresses meaning is not to penetrate beyond the image itself.
value.literal: Now to say that establishing images fully expresses meaning — this does not penetrate beyond the image.

value.zh: 繫辭焉以盡言，此非言乎繫表者也；
value.en: Attaching words to fully express speech is not to speak of what is merely attached to the surface;
value.literal: Attaching words to fully express speech — this is not speaking of what is attached to the surface;

value.zh: 斯則象外之意，繫表之言，固蘊而不出矣。」
value.en: the meaning beyond the images and the words beyond the surface are inherently contained and do not emerge."
value.literal: then the meaning beyond the image and the words attached to the surface are originally hidden and do not emerge."

value.zh: 及當時能言者不能屈也。
value.en: At the time, none of the leading debaters could defeat him.
value.literal: At the time, those skilled in discourse could not refute him.

value.zh: 又論父彧不如從兄攸。
value.en: He also argued that his father Yu was inferior to his cousin Xun You.
value.literal: He also argued that his father Yu was not equal to his cousin You.

value.zh: 彧立德髙整，軌儀以訓物，而攸不治外形，愼密自居而已。
value.en: Yu's virtue was lofty and orderly, teaching others through standard and ceremony; Xun You did not cultivate appearances outwardly, contenting himself with careful inward reserve.
value.literal: Yu established virtue that was lofty and ordered, using standards and ceremony to instruct things; You did not cultivate external appearance, merely keeping careful secrecy to himself.

value.zh: 粲以此言善攸，諸兄怒而不能迴也。
value.en: Can used this argument to praise Xun You; his elder brothers were furious but could not change his mind.
value.literal: Can with these words praised You; his elder brothers were angry but could not turn him back.

value.zh: 太和初，到京邑與傅嘏談。
value.en: Early in the Taihe reign, he came to the capital and discussed philosophy with Fu Gu.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign, he arrived at the capital and conversed with Fu Gu.

value.zh: 嘏善名理而粲尚玄遠，宗致雖同，倉卒時或有格而不相得意。
value.en: Fu Gu excelled at logical disputation while Can favored the abstruse and metaphysical; though they shared fundamental aims, in quick exchanges they sometimes clashed and failed to understand each other.
value.literal: Gu was skilled in the principles of naming while Can esteemed the abstruse and far-reaching; although their fundamental aims were the same, in hasty moments there were sometimes clashes and mutual incomprehension.

value.zh: 裴徽通彼我之懷，爲二家騎驛，頃之，粲與嘏善。
value.en: Pei Hui understood both men's perspectives and mediated between them; before long, Can and Fu Gu became friends.
value.literal: Pei Hui understood the feelings of both sides and served as a relay rider between the two schools; shortly thereafter, Can and Gu became friends.

value.zh: 夏侯玄亦親。
value.en: He was also close to Xiahou Xuan.
value.literal: Xiahou Xuan was also close to him.

value.zh: 常謂嘏、玄曰：「子等在世塗間，功名必勝我，但識劣我耳！」
value.en: He often told Fu Gu and Xiahou Xuan: "You will surpass me in worldly fame and achievement, but your understanding falls short of mine!"
value.literal: He often said to Gu and Xuan: "You gentlemen on the path of worldly life — your fame and achievement will surely surpass mine, but your insight is inferior to mine!"

value.zh: 嘏難曰：「能盛功名者，識也。
value.en: Fu Gu objected: "It is insight that produces great fame and achievement.
value.literal: Gu challenged him, saying: "Those who can flourish in fame and achievement — that is insight.

value.zh: 天下孰有本不足而末有餘者邪？」
value.en: Who in the world has a weak foundation but abundant fruit?"
value.literal: In all the world, is there anyone whose root is insufficient yet whose branches are abundant?"

value.zh: 粲曰：「功名者，志局之所獎也。
value.en: Can replied: "Fame and achievement are the rewards of ambition and vision.
value.literal: Can said: "Fame and achievement are what ambition and design reward.

value.zh: 然則志局自一物耳，固非識之所獨濟也。
value.en: Ambition and vision are one thing — they are not achieved by insight alone.
value.literal: Thus ambition and design are themselves one thing; they are certainly not what insight alone can accomplish.

value.zh: 我以能使子等爲貴，然未必齊子等所爲也。」
value.en: I take pride in being able to make men like you succeed, yet I may not equal what men like you achieve."
value.literal: I take as my honor that I can make gentlemen like you succeed, yet I am not necessarily equal to what gentlemen like you accomplish."

value.zh: 粲常以婦人者，才智不足論，自宜以色爲主。
value.en: Can often said that a woman's intellect was not worth discussing — beauty was what mattered.
value.literal: Can often held that as for women, intellectual talent was not worth discussing; they should naturally take beauty as their main quality.

value.zh: 驃騎將軍曹洪女有美色，粲於是娉焉，容服帷帳甚麗，專房歡宴。
value.en: The daughter of General of Agile Cavalry Cao Hong was renowned for her beauty; Can married her, furnishing their private chamber lavishly and devoting himself to her exclusively.
value.literal: The daughter of General of Agile Cavalry Cao Hong had beautiful looks; Can therefore married her; her dress, furnishings, and curtains were very sumptuous; he kept her in a private chamber for joyous feasting.

value.zh: 歴年後，婦病亡，未殯，傅嘏往喭粲；
value.en: After several years his wife died of illness; before the funeral, Fu Gu came to console Can;
value.literal: After some years, his wife died of illness; before the burial, Fu Gu went to console Can;

value.zh: 粲不哭而神傷。
value.en: Can did not weep outwardly, but his spirit was crushed.
value.literal: Can did not weep but his spirit was wounded.

value.zh: 嘏問曰：「婦人才色並茂爲難。
value.en: Fu Gu asked: "It is rare for a woman to possess both talent and beauty.
value.literal: Gu asked, saying: "For a woman to possess both talent and beauty in abundance is difficult.

value.zh: 子之娶也，遺才而好色。
value.en: In marrying, you set aside talent and chose beauty alone.
value.literal: In your marriage, you left aside talent and favored beauty.

value.zh: 此自易遇，今何哀之甚？」
value.en: That should be easy to replace — why grieve so deeply?"
value.literal: This is itself easy to encounter — why grieve so deeply now?"

value.zh: 粲曰：「佳人難再得！
value.en: Can said: "A woman of such beauty cannot be found again!
value.literal: Can said: "A beautiful woman is hard to obtain again!

value.zh: 顧逝者不能有傾國之色，然未可謂之易遇。」
value.en: She may not have had nation-toppling beauty, but one still cannot call her easy to replace."
value.literal: Looking at the departed, she could not possess nation-toppling beauty, yet one still cannot say she was easy to encounter."

value.zh: 痛悼不能已，歳餘亦亡，時年二十九。
value.en: He could not recover from his grief; a little over a year later he too died, at the age of twenty-nine.
value.literal: His grief could not cease; after a little more than a year he also died, aged twenty-nine at the time.

value.zh: 粲簡貴，不能與常人交接，所交皆一時俊傑。
value.en: Can was refined and aloof; he could not mix with ordinary people and associated only with the age's finest minds.
value.literal: Can was refined and noble; he could not associate with ordinary people; those he associated with were all outstanding talents of the age.

value.zh: 至葬夕，赴者裁十餘人，皆同時知名士也，哭之，感慟路人。
value.en: On the night of his burial, only a dozen or so mourners came — all distinguished men of the day — and their weeping moved passersby to tears.
value.literal: On the evening of the burial, those who came numbered only a little more than ten — all were well-known scholars of the time; when they wept for him, passersby were moved to grief.

value.zh: 惲子甝，嗣爲散騎常侍，進爵廣陽鄕侯，年三十薨。
value.en: Yun's son Kan succeeded him as Regular Attendant of the Central Secretariat, was advanced to Marquis of Guangyang Township, and died at thirty.
value.literal: Yun's son Kan succeeded and served as Regular Attendant of the Central Secretariat; he was advanced to Marquis of Guangyang Township and died at age thirty.

value.zh: 子頵嗣。
value.en: His son Yin succeeded him.
value.literal: His son Yin succeeded.

value.zh: 《荀氏家傳》曰：頵字温伯，爲羽林右監，早卒。
value.en: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan records that Yin styled Wenbo, served as Right Director of the Forest of Feathers, and died young.
value.literal: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan states: Yin's style name was Wenbo; he served as Right Director of the Forest of Feathers and died young.

value.zh: 頵子崧，字景猷。
value.en: Yin's son Song styled Jingyou.
value.literal: Yin's son Song's style name was Jingyou.

value.zh: 《晉陽秋》稱崧少有志操，雅好文學，孝義和愛，在朝恪勤，位至左右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
value.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Jin praises Song as a youth of noble aspiration, devoted to literature, filial and compassionate; diligent in office, he rose to Household Grandee of the Left and Right and Grand Master with Imperial Carriage Honors.
value.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals of Jin praises Song as having lofty aspirations and conduct from youth, elegantly loving literature, filial, righteous, harmonious, and loving; in court he was diligent and careful, reaching the offices of Left and Right Household Grandee and Grand Master with the Honours of an Imperial Carriage and the Three Dignities.

value.zh: 崧子羨，字令則，淸和有才。
value.en: Song's son Xian styled Lingze — refined, harmonious, and talented.
value.literal: Song's son Xian's style name was Lingze; he was pure and harmonious and possessed talent.

value.zh: 尚公主，少歴顯位，年二十八爲北中郎將，徐、兖二州刺史，假節都督徐、兖、靑三州諸軍事。
value.en: He married an imperial princess, held distinguished office from youth, and at twenty-eight became General of the North and Central, Governor of Xu and Yan Provinces, with credentials of authority as Commander of military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing.
value.literal: He married an imperial princess; from youth he passed through distinguished offices; at age twenty-eight he was General of the North and Central, Governor of Xu and Yan Provinces, and Provisionally bearing credentials of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing Provinces.

value.zh: 在任十年，遇疾解職，卒於家，追贈驃騎將軍。
value.en: After ten years in office he fell ill and resigned; he died at home and was posthumously awarded the rank of General of Agile Cavalry.
value.literal: During ten years in office, he encountered illness and resigned his post; he died at home and was posthumously granted the office of General of Agile Cavalry.

value.zh: 羨孫伯子，今御史中丞也。
value.en: Xian's grandson Bozi is the present Censor-in-Chief.
value.literal: Xian's grandson Bozi — the present Censor-in-Chief.

value.zh: 霬官至中領軍，薨，諡曰貞侯，追贈驃騎將軍。
value.en: Hui rose to Central Army Inspector; he died and was posthumously titled Marquis Zhen and awarded the rank of General of Agile Cavalry.
value.literal: Hui reached the office of Central Army Inspector; he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhen; he was posthumously granted the office of General of Agile Cavalry.

value.zh: 子愷嗣。
value.en: His son Kai succeeded him.
value.literal: His son Kai succeeded.

value.zh: 霬妻，司馬景王、文王之妹也，二王皆與親善。
value.en: Hui's wife was the younger sister of the Kings of Jing and Wen (Sima Shi and Sima Zhao); both Sima brothers were on close terms with the family.
value.literal: Hui's wife was the younger sister of Sima the King of Jing and Sima the King of Wen; both kings were on close and friendly terms with him.

value.zh: 咸熙中，開建五等，霬以著勳前朝，改封愷南頓子。
value.en: During Xianxi, when the five noble ranks were established, Kai was enfeoffed as Viscount of Nandun in recognition of Hui's merit under the previous dynasty.
value.literal: In the Xianxi period, when the five ranks of nobility were established, because Hui had displayed merit in the previous dynasty, Kai was changed in enfeoffment to Viscount of Nandun.

value.zh: 《荀氏家傳》曰：愷，晉武帝時爲侍中。
value.en: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan records that Kai served as Palace Attendant under Emperor Wu of Jin.
value.literal: The Genealogical Biography of the Xun Clan states: Kai served as Palace Attendant under Emperor Wu of Jin.

value.zh: 干寶《晉紀》曰：武帝使侍中荀顗、和嶠倶至東宮，觀察太子。
value.en: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin records that Emperor Wu sent Palace Attendants Xun Yi and He Qiao together to the Eastern Palace to observe the Crown Prince.
value.literal: Gan Bao's Annals of Jin states: Emperor Wu sent Palace Attendants Xun Yi and He Qiao together to the Eastern Palace to observe the Crown Prince.

value.zh: 顗還稱太子德識進茂，而嶠云聖質如初。
value.en: On returning, Yi reported that the Crown Prince's virtue and insight were flourishing; He Qiao said his sage-like qualities were unchanged.
value.literal: When Yi returned, he praised the Crown Prince's virtue and insight as advancing and flourishing; He Qiao said his sage-like quality was as at first.

value.zh: 孫盛曰「遣荀勗」，其餘語則同。
value.en: Sun Sheng writes "sent Xun Xu"; the rest is the same.
value.literal: Sun Sheng says "sent Xun Xu"; the rest of the wording is the same.

value.zh: 臣松之案和嶠爲侍中，荀顗亡沒久矣。
value.en: Pei Songzhi notes: He Qiao was Palace Attendant, but Xun Yi had long been dead.
value.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: He Qiao served as Palace Attendant; Xun Yi had long since died.

value.zh: 荀勗位亞台司，不與嶠同班，無縁方稱侍中。
value.en: Xun Xu ranked just below the chief ministers and was not in He Qiao's cohort — he could not have been called simply "Palace Attendant."
value.literal: Xun Xu's position was second to the ministers of the Terrace; he was not in the same rank as Qiao; there was no reason he would be called Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 二書所云，皆爲非也。
value.en: Both accounts are wrong.
value.literal: What both books say is all incorrect.

value.zh: 考其時位，愷寔當之。
value.en: Considering the dates and offices involved, Kai must have been the man.
value.literal: Examining the times and positions, Kai truly should have been the one.

value.zh: 愷位至征西大將軍。
value.en: Kai rose to General Who Conquers the West.
value.literal: Kai reached the office of General Who Conquers the West.

value.zh: 愷兄憺，少府。
value.en: Kai's elder brother Dan served as Minister Steward.
value.literal: Kai's elder brother Dan — Minister Steward.

value.zh: 弟悝，護軍將軍，追贈車騎大將軍。
value.en: His younger brother Kui served as General Who Guards the Army and was posthumously awarded the rank of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
value.literal: His younger brother Kui — General Who Guards the Army; posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry.

value.zh: 列傳第十九 殷淳子孚弟沖淡張暢何偃江智淵
value.en: Biography 19: Yin Chun, Yin Fu, Yin Chong, Yin Dan, Zhang Chang, He Yan, and Jiang Zhiyuan
value.literal: Biography 19: Yin Chun, his son Fu, younger brothers Chong and Dan, Zhang Chang, He Yan, Jiang Zhiyuan

value.zh: 史臣曰：夫將帥者，御眾之名；
value.en: The historian remarks: The term "commander" denotes one who governs troops;
value.literal: The historian says: A commander is the name for one who governs the multitude;

value.zh: 士卒者，一夫之用。
value.en: soldiers are the instrument of a single man.
value.literal: soldiers are the use of a single man.

value.zh: 坐談兵機，制勝千里，安在乎蒙楯前驅，履腸涉血而已哉！
value.en: To sit and discuss strategy and prevail a thousand li away — what need is there merely to bear a shield in the van and tread through blood and entrails!
value.literal: To sit and discuss military stratagem, to overcome a thousand li away — how does that depend on bearing a shield and driving ahead, treading entrails and wading through blood alone!

value.zh: 山濤之稱羊祜曰：「大將雖不須筋力，軍中猶宜強健。」
value.en: Shan Tao said of Yang Hu, "A great general need not rely on brute strength, yet in the army robust health is still desirable."
value.literal: Shan Tao's praise of Yang Hu said: "A great general may not need physical strength, yet in the army one should still be robust."

value.zh: 以此為言，則叔子之幹力弱矣。
value.en: By that standard, Shuzi's physical vigor was slight.
value.literal: By this saying, then Shuzi's physical strength was weak.

value.zh: 杜預文士儒生，身不能穿札，射未嘗跨馬，一朝統大眾二十餘萬，為平吳都督。
value.en: Du Yu was a literati and Confucian scholar who could not pierce a target with an arrow and had never mounted a horse for archery — yet one morning he took command of more than two hundred thousand men as director-general for the conquest of Wu.
value.literal: Du Yu was a literary scholar and Confucian student — his body could not pierce a target; in archery he had never straddled a horse — yet in a morning he commanded a great host of more than two hundred thousand as Director-General for the Pacification of Wu.

value.zh: 王戎把臂入林，亦受專征之寄。
value.en: Wang Rong, the man who linked arms with Ruan Ji in the bamboo grove, likewise received an independent military command.
value.literal: Wang Rong, arm in arm entering the grove, also received the entrustment of independent campaign command.

value.zh: 何必山西猛士，六郡良家，然後可受脤於朝堂，荷推轂之重。
value.en: Why must one be a fierce warrior of Shanxi or a son of a good family from the six commanderies before receiving investiture at court and bearing the weight of supreme command?
value.literal: Why must there be fierce warriors of Shanxi and good families of the six commanderies before one may receive sacrificial flesh in the court hall and bear the weight of the chariot-push?

value.zh: 及虜兵深入，徐服恇震，非張暢正言，則彭、汴危矣。
value.en: When the barbarian armies drove deep inland and Xu Province trembled with fear, had it not been for Zhang Chang's forthright counsel, Pengcheng and Bian would have been lost.
value.literal: When the barbarian armies penetrated deep, Xu and the coastal regions were shaken with fear — had it not been for Zhang Chang's upright words, Peng and Bian would have been in peril.

value.zh: 豈其身捍飛鏑，手折雲衝，方足使窮揲假命，危城載安乎？
value.en: Was it only by catching flying bolts with his body or snapping siege engines with his hands that he saved a doomed city and a desperate garrison?
value.literal: Was it only by his body blocking flying bolts and his hands breaking cloud-chariots that he could make the desperate divination gain life and the perilous city bear peace?

value.zh: 仁者之有勇，非為臆說。
value.en: That the benevolent can also be brave is no idle speculation.
value.literal: That the benevolent also have courage is no fanciful doctrine.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 倫陰與秀謀篡位，欲先除朝望，且報宿怨，乃執張華、裴頠、解系、解結等於殿前。
value.en: Lun secretly plotted usurpation with Xiu, first removing leading ministers and settling old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others in the hall.
value.literal: Lun secretly plotted with Xiu to usurp the throne, wishing first to remove men of court esteem and also settle old scores; he seized Zhang Hua, Pei Wei, Xie Ji, Xie Jie, and others before the hall.

value.zh: 華謂張林曰：「卿欲害忠臣邪？」
value.en: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you mean to kill loyal ministers?"
value.literal: Hua said to Zhang Lin: "Do you wish to harm loyal ministers?"

value.zh: 林稱詔詰之曰：「卿為宰相，太子之廢，不能死節，何也？」
value.en: Lin, citing the edict, demanded: "As chief minister, when the heir apparent was deposed why did you not die for principle?"
value.literal: Lin, claiming the edict, interrogated him: "You were chief minister; when the Heir Apparent was deposed you could not die for principle—why?"

value.zh: 華曰：「式乾之議，臣諫事具存，可覆按也。」
value.en: Hua said: "My remonstrance at the Shiqian deliberation is on record and may be reviewed."
value.literal: Hua said: "On the deliberation at Shiqian my remonstrance is fully recorded and may be reviewed."

value.zh: 林曰：「諫而不從，何不去位？」
value.en: Lin said: "If remonstrance failed, why not resign?"
value.literal: Lin said: "If you remonstrated and were not obeyed, why not leave office?"

value.zh: 華無以對。
value.en: Hua had no answer.
value.literal: Hua had no reply.

value.zh: 遂皆斬之，仍夷三族。
value.en: All were beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.
value.literal: They were all beheaded and their clans exterminated to the third degree.

value.zh: 解結女適裴氏，明日當嫁而禍起，裴氏欲認活之，女曰：「家既若此，我何以活為！」
value.en: Xie Jie's daughter was to marry into the Pei clan next day when disaster struck; the Peis wished to save her; she said: "With my house destroyed, how can I live!"
value.literal: Xie Jie's daughter was betrothed to the Pei clan; the wedding was due the next day when disaster struck; the Pei wished to claim her alive; the girl said: "With my house thus, how can I live!"

value.zh: 亦坐死。
value.en: She died as well.
value.literal: She too died for it.

value.zh: 朝廷由是議革舊制，女不從死。
value.en: The court then debated abolishing the old rule that wives and daughters die with the clan.
value.literal: The court thereupon debated abolishing the old rule that daughters follow their kin to death.

value.zh: 甲午，倫坐端門，遣尚書和郁持節送賈庶人於金墉；
value.en: On jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed empress to Jinyong;
value.literal: On the day jiawu Lun sat at the Duan Gate and sent the Masters of Writing He Yu with credentials to convey the deposed Jia commoner to Jinyong;

value.zh: 誅劉振、董猛、孫慮、程據等；
value.en: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;
value.literal: Liu Zhen, Dong Meng, Sun Lv, Cheng Ju, and others were executed;

value.zh: 司徒王戎及內外官坐張、裴親黨黜免者甚眾。
value.en: Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and many inner and outer officials were dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei.
value.literal: the Minister over the Masses Wang Rong and inner and outer officials dismissed as kin to Zhang and Pei were very numerous.

value.zh: 閻纘撫張華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也！」
value.en: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I urged you to resign and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"
value.literal: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I told you early to yield your post and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"
